passages.translation_en: Chen Zhen asked: "Previously in Qi, the king offered you a gift of one hundred yi of fine gold and you refused it. In Song, you were offered seventy yi and accepted. In Xue, you were offered fifty yi and accepted. If the earlier refusal was right, then the later acceptances were wrong; if the later acceptances were right, then the earlier refusal was wrong. Master, it must be one or the other." Mencius said: "Both were right. When I was in Song, I was about to go on a long journey. For a traveler, one gives a travel gift. The accompanying words were: 'A gift for your journey.' Why should I not accept? When I was in Xue, I was on guard for my safety. The words were: 'I have heard you are taking precautions, so here is money for arms.' Why should I not accept? But in Qi, there was no such occasion. To give a gift without occasion is to buy someone off. How could a gentleman allow himself to be bought?"

passages.text: 孟子之平陸。謂其大夫曰：「子之持戟之士，一日而三失伍，則去之否乎？」曰：「不待三。」「然則子之失伍也亦多矣。凶年饑歲，子之民，老羸轉於溝壑，壯者散而之四方者，幾千人矣。」曰：「此非距心之所得為也。」曰：「今有受人之牛羊而為之牧之者，則必為之求牧與芻矣。求牧與芻而不得，則反諸其人乎？抑亦立而視其死與？」曰：「此則距心之罪也。」
passages.translation_en: Mencius went to Pinlu and said to its governor: "If one of your soldiers deserted his post three times in a single day, would you dismiss him?" The governor said: "I would not wait for three times." "But you yourself have deserted your post many times over. In years of famine and hardship, your people — the old and weak left dying in ditches, the able-bodied scattered to the four directions — have numbered in the thousands." The governor said: "This is not something that I, Ju Xin, have the power to remedy." Mencius said: "Suppose someone were entrusted with another person's cattle and sheep to tend. He would surely need to find pasture and fodder for them. If he could not find pasture and fodder, would he return the animals to their owner, or would he simply stand by and watch them die?" The governor said: "This is indeed my fault."

passages.text: 他日，見於王曰：「王之為都者，臣知五人焉。知其罪者，惟孔距心。為王誦之。」王曰：「此則寡人之罪也。」孟子謂蚔鼃曰：「子之辭靈丘而請士師，似也，為其可以言也。今既數月矣，未可以言與？」蚔鼃諫於王而不用，致為臣而去。齊人曰：「所以為蚔鼃，則善矣；所以自為，則吾不知也。」公都子以告。曰：「吾聞之也：有官守者，不得其職則去；有言責者，不得其言則去。我無官守，我無言責也，則吾進退，豈不綽綽然有餘裕哉？」
passages.translation_en: Another day, Mencius had an audience with the king and said: "Among Your Majesty's city governors, I know five. The only one who recognizes his own failings is Kong Juxin." He recounted the conversation for the king. The king said: "In that case, the fault is mine." Mencius then said to Chi Wa: "You resigned from the governorship of Lingqiu and requested the post of Chief Justice — that seemed reasonable, since the position would give you the standing to speak up. Now several months have passed — have you still not been able to speak?" Chi Wa remonstrated with the king but was ignored, so he resigned his office and left. The people of Qi said: "What he did for Chi Wa was well done, but what he did for himself — that we do not understand." When Gongduzi reported this to Mencius, he said: "I have heard it said: He who holds an office leaves when he cannot fulfill its duties; he who bears the responsibility of counsel leaves when his words go unheeded. I hold no office and bear no responsibility for counsel — so in my comings and goings, am I not perfectly free and at ease?"

passages.text: 孟子為卿於齊，出吊於滕，王使蓋大夫王驩為輔行。王驩朝暮見，反齊滕之路，未嘗與之言行事也。公孫丑曰：「齊卿之位，不為小矣；齊滕之路，不為近矣。反之而未嘗與言行事，何也？」曰：「夫既或治之，予何言哉？」孟子自齊葬於魯，反於齊，止於嬴。充虞請曰：「前日不知虞之不肖，使虞敦匠事。嚴，虞不敢請。今願竊有請也，木若以美然。」
passages.translation_en: When Mencius was a minister in Qi, he was sent on a condolence mission to Teng. The king appointed Gai's governor, Wang Huan, as his escort. Wang Huan called on him morning and evening, but throughout the journey between Qi and Teng, Mencius never once discussed the affairs of the mission with him. Gongsun Chou said: "The position of a Qi minister is not insignificant, and the road between Qi and Teng is not short. Yet you traveled back and forth without ever discussing the mission with him — why?" Mencius said: "He had already taken charge of everything himself. What was there for me to say?" When Mencius returned from burying his mother in Lu and was back in Qi, he stopped at Ying. Chong Yu said: "Previously, not knowing how unworthy I was, you entrusted me with managing the coffin construction. At that solemn time I did not dare raise questions. Now I would like to ask: didn't the wood seem rather fine?"

passages.text: 曰：「古者棺槨無度，中古棺七寸，槨稱之。自天子達於庶人。非直為觀美也，然後盡於人心。不得，不可以為悅；無財，不可以為悅。得之為有財，古之人皆用之，吾何為獨不然？且比化者，無使土親膚，於人心獨無恔乎？吾聞之君子：不以天下儉其親。」沈同以其私問曰：「燕可伐與？」
passages.translation_en: Mencius said: "In ancient times there were no fixed standards for inner and outer coffins. In the middle period, the inner coffin was seven inches thick, and the outer coffin proportionate. This applied from the Son of Heaven down to commoners. It was not merely for the sake of appearance — only then could people fully express their feelings. If prevented by regulations, they could not be satisfied; if lacking the means, they could not be satisfied. When both permission and means were available, the ancients all did it — why should I alone do otherwise? Moreover, is there not some comfort to the bereaved in ensuring that bare earth does not touch the skin of the deceased? I have heard that a gentleman does not stint on his parents for the sake of the world." Shen Tong asked him privately: "May Yan be attacked?"

passages.text: 孟子曰：「可。子噲不得與人燕，子之不得受燕於子噲。有仕於此，而子悅之，不告於王而私與之吾子之祿爵；夫士也，亦無王命而私受之於子，則可乎？何以異於是？」齊人伐燕。或問曰：「勸齊伐燕，有諸？」
passages.translation_en: Mencius said: "Yes, it may. Zi Kuai had no right to give Yan to another person, and Zi Zhi had no right to accept Yan from Zi Kuai. Suppose there were an official here whom you were pleased with. Without informing the king, you privately gave him your own salary and rank; and suppose that official, also without royal authorization, privately accepted it from you — would that be permissible? How is the case of Yan any different?" When Qi attacked Yan, someone asked: "Is it true that you urged Qi to attack Yan?"

passages.text: 曰：「未也。沈同問『燕可伐與』？吾應之曰『可』，彼然而伐之也。彼如曰『孰可以伐之』？則將應之曰：『為天吏，則可以伐之。』今有殺人者，或問之曰『人可殺與』？則將應之曰『可』。彼如曰『孰可以殺之』？則將應之曰：『為士師，則可以殺之。』今以燕伐燕，何為勸之哉？」燕人畔。王曰：「吾甚慚於孟子。」陳賈曰：「王無患焉。王自以為與周公，孰仁且智？」王曰：「惡！是何言也？」
passages.translation_en: Mencius said: "No. Shen Tong asked, 'May Yan be attacked?' I answered, 'Yes,' and they went ahead and attacked. But if he had asked, 'Who may attack it?' I would have answered: 'Only one acting as Heaven's agent may attack it.' It is like this: if someone commits murder and another asks, 'May this person be killed?' I would answer, 'Yes.' But if asked, 'Who may kill him?' I would answer: 'Only the Chief Justice may kill him.' Now Qi attacked Yan — this was one Yan attacking another Yan. Why would I have urged that?" The people of Yan rebelled. The king said: "I am deeply ashamed before Mencius." Chen Jia said: "Your Majesty need not worry. Does Your Majesty consider himself more benevolent and wise than the Duke of Zhou?" The king said: "What! What kind of talk is that?"

passages.text: 曰：「周公使管叔監殷，管叔以殷畔。知而使之，是不仁也；不知而使之，是不智也。仁智，周公未之盡也，而況於王乎？賈請見而解之。」見孟子，問曰：「周公何人也？」曰：「古聖人也。」曰：「使管叔監殷，管叔以殷畔也，有諸？」曰：「然。」曰：「周公知其將畔而使之與？」曰：「不知也。」「然則聖人且有過與？」
passages.translation_en: Chen Jia said: "The Duke of Zhou appointed his brother Guan Shu to oversee the Yin remnants, and Guan Shu used the Yin people to rebel. If the Duke of Zhou knew he would rebel and still appointed him, that was a lack of benevolence. If he did not know, that was a lack of wisdom. Even the Duke of Zhou did not fully attain benevolence and wisdom — how much less can be expected of Your Majesty? Allow me to go see Mencius and explain this." He went to see Mencius and asked: "What sort of man was the Duke of Zhou?" Mencius said: "A sage of antiquity." "He appointed Guan Shu to oversee the Yin remnants, and Guan Shu used them to rebel — is this true?" "It is." "Did the Duke of Zhou know he would rebel when he appointed him?" "He did not know." "Then even a sage makes mistakes?"

passages.text: 曰：「周公，弟也；管叔，兄也。周公之過，不亦宜乎？且古之君子，過則改之；今之君子，過則順之。古之君子，其過也，如日月之食，民皆見之；及其更也，民皆仰之。今之君子，豈徒順之，又從為之辭。」孟子致為臣而歸。王就見孟子，曰：「前日願見而不可得，得侍，同朝甚喜。今又棄寡人而歸，不識可以繼此而得見乎？」對曰：「不敢請耳，固所願也。」
passages.translation_en: Mencius said: "The Duke of Zhou was the younger brother; Guan Shu was the elder. Was not the Duke of Zhou's mistake understandable? Moreover, when gentlemen of old made mistakes, they corrected them. Gentlemen of today, when they make mistakes, persist in them. The mistakes of gentlemen of old were like eclipses of the sun or moon — the people all saw them; and when they corrected them, the people all looked up to them with admiration. Gentlemen of today not only persist in their errors but go on to make excuses for them." Mencius resigned his office and returned home. The king came to see him and said: "Previously I wished to see you but could not. Then I was delighted to serve alongside you at court. Now you are abandoning me and going home. May I hope to see you again hereafter?" Mencius replied: "I would not presume to request it, but it is certainly my wish."

passages.text: 他日，王謂時子曰：「我欲中國而授孟子室，養弟子以萬鍾，使諸大夫國人皆有所矜式。子盍為我言之？」
passages.translation_en: Another day, the king said to Shi Zi: "I wish to give Mencius a house in the center of the capital, and to support his disciples with a stipend of ten thousand zhong of grain, so that all the officials and people will have someone to look up to and emulate. Would you convey this to him for me?"

passages.text: 時子因陳子而以告孟子，陳子以時子之言告孟子。孟子曰：「然。夫時子惡知其不可也？如使予欲富，辭十萬而受萬，是為欲富乎？季孫曰：『異哉子叔疑！使己為政，不用，則亦已矣，又使其子弟為卿。人亦孰不欲富貴？而獨於富貴之中，有私龍斷焉。』古之為市也，以其所有易其所無者，有司者治之耳。有賤丈夫焉，必求龍斷而登之，以左右望而罔市利。人皆以為賤，故從而征之。征商，自此賤丈夫始矣。孟子去齊，宿於晝。
passages.translation_en: Shi Zi relayed the message through Chen Zi, and Chen Zi told Mencius. Mencius said: "Very well. But how would Shi Zi know that this cannot be done? If I desired wealth, would I have refused a hundred thousand and accepted ten thousand — is that the behavior of someone who desires wealth? Ji Sun once said: 'How strange is Zi Shu Yi! He pushed himself into government, and when he was not employed, that should have been the end of it. But then he got his sons and brothers appointed as ministers. Who does not desire wealth and rank? But he cornered the market on wealth and rank all by himself.' In ancient times, the marketplace was simply a place where people exchanged what they had for what they lacked, overseen by an official. But there was a base fellow who would always seek out a prominent mound to climb, looking left and right to snare all the profit in the market. Everyone thought him contemptible, and so they taxed him. The taxation of merchants began with this base fellow." Mencius left Qi and lodged at Zhou.

passages.text: 有欲為王留行者，坐而言。不應，隱几而臥。客不悅曰：「弟子齊宿而後敢言，夫子臥而不聽，請勿復敢見矣。」曰：「坐！我明語子。昔者魯繆公無人乎子思之側，則不能安子思；泄柳、申詳，無人乎繆公之側，則不能安其身。子為長者慮，而不及子思，子絕長者乎？長者絕子乎？」
passages.translation_en: Someone who wanted to persuade the king to detain Mencius sat down and began to speak. Mencius did not respond, but leaned on his armrest and dozed. The visitor was displeased and said: "I purified myself with a night of fasting before daring to speak, yet you doze and do not listen. I shall never presume to see you again." Mencius said: "Sit down! Let me speak plainly. In the past, if Duke Mu of Lu did not have a trusted person at Zi Si's side, he could not have kept Zi Si at ease. And if Xie Liu and Shen Xiang had not had trusted people at Duke Mu's side, they could not have kept themselves secure. You presume to plan on behalf of an elder, yet your concern does not match what Zi Si received. Is it you who are cutting off the elder, or is it the elder who is cutting you off?"

passages.text: 孟子去齊。尹士語人曰：「不識王之不可以為湯武，則是不明也；識其不可，然且至，則是干澤也。千里而見王，不遇故去。三宿而後出晝，是何濡滯也？士則茲不悅。」
passages.translation_en: Mencius left Qi. Yin Shi said to others: "If he did not realize that the king could not become a Tang or a Wu, then he is not perceptive. If he realized it yet still came, then he was just angling for gain. He traveled a thousand li to see the king; finding him unreceptive, he left. Yet he lingered three nights before departing Zhou — why was he so slow? This is what I find displeasing."

passages.text: 高子以告。曰：「夫尹士惡知予哉？千里而見王，是予所欲也；不遇故去，豈予所欲哉？予不得已也。予三宿而出晝，於予心猶以為速。王庶幾改之。王如改諸，則必反予。夫出晝而王不予追也，予然後浩然有歸志。予雖然，豈舍王哉？王由足用為善。王如用予，則豈徒齊民安，天下之民舉安。王庶幾改之，予日望之。予豈若是小丈夫然哉？諫於其君而不受，則怒，悻悻然見於其面。去則窮日之力而後宿哉？」尹士聞之曰：「士誠小人也。」
passages.translation_en: Gao Zi reported this to Mencius. Mencius said: "How could Yin Shi understand me? I traveled a thousand li to see the king — that was what I desired. To leave because I was not received — was that what I desired? I had no choice. I stayed three nights before leaving Zhou, and in my heart I still felt it was too soon. I hoped the king might yet change his mind. If the king had changed, he would surely have called me back. Only when I left Zhou and the king did not send after me did I finally resolve wholeheartedly to go home. But even so, how could I give up on the king? The king is still capable of doing good. If the king were to use me, it would not be just the people of Qi who would find peace — the people of the whole world would find peace. I kept hoping the king might change. Every day I watched for it. Do you think I am like some petty man who, when his remonstrance to his ruler is rejected, gets angry, shows his resentment on his face, and when he leaves, exhausts a whole day's travel before stopping for the night?" When Yin Shi heard this, he said: "I am truly a small man."

passages.text: 孟子去齊。充虞路問曰：「夫子若有不豫色然。前日虞聞諸夫子曰：『君子不怨天，不尤人。』」曰：「彼一時，此一時也。五百年必有王者興，其間必有名世者。由周而來，七百有餘歲矣。以其數則過矣，以其時考之則可矣。夫天，未欲平治天下也；如欲平治天下，當今之世，舍我其誰也？吾何為不豫哉？」孟子去齊，居休。公孫丑問曰：「仕而不受祿，古之道乎？」
passages.translation_en: Mencius left Qi. Chong Yu asked him on the road: "Master, you seem to have an unhappy expression. The other day I heard you say: 'A gentleman does not blame Heaven or resent others.'" Mencius said: "That was one time; this is another. Every five hundred years a true king must arise, and in the interval there must be those who are renowned in their age. From the Zhou dynasty to now, it has been over seven hundred years. By the count, the time is overdue; by the circumstances, the moment is right. But Heaven does not yet wish to bring peace and order to the world. If it did wish to bring peace and order to the world, who in this present age is there besides me? Why should I be unhappy?" Mencius left Qi and settled in Xiu. Gongsun Chou asked: "To serve in office yet not accept a salary — is that the Way of the ancients?"

passages.text: 曰：「非也。於崇，吾得見王。退而有去志，不欲變，故不受也。繼而有師命，不可以請。久於齊，非我志也。」
passages.translation_en: Mencius said: "No. At Chong, I obtained an audience with the king. When I withdrew, I already had the intention to leave, and I did not wish to change that intention — so I did not accept a salary. Then military orders came, and I could not request leave. My long stay in Qi was not what I had intended."

passages.text: 滕文公為世子，將之楚，過宋而見孟子。孟子道性善，言必稱堯舜。世子自楚反，復見孟子。孟子曰：「世子疑吾言乎？夫道一而已矣。成覸謂齊景公曰：『彼丈夫也，我丈夫也，吾何畏彼哉？』顏淵曰：『舜何人也？予何人也？有為者亦若是。』公明儀曰：『文王我師也，周公豈欺我哉？』今滕，絕長補短，將五十里也，猶可以為善國。《書》曰：『若藥不瞑眩，厥疾不瘳。』」
passages.translation_en: When Duke Wen of Teng was still heir apparent, he was traveling to Chu and passed through Song, where he met Mencius. Mencius spoke to him about the goodness of human nature, and in every instance cited Yao and Shun as examples. On his way back from Chu, the heir apparent visited Mencius again. Mencius said, 'Do you doubt my words? The Way is one and only one. Cheng Jian said to Duke Jing of Qi: "He is a man and I am a man — why should I be in awe of him?" Yan Yuan said: "What sort of man was Shun? What sort of man am I? Anyone who makes the effort can become like him." Gongming Yi said: "King Wen is my teacher — how could the Duke of Zhou deceive me?" Now Teng, if you trim the long and patch the short, has a territory of about fifty li square. It can still become a good state. The Book of Documents says: "If the medicine does not make you dizzy and nauseous, the illness will not be cured."'

passages.text: 滕定公薨。世子謂然友曰：「昔者孟子嘗與我言於宋，於心終不忘。今也不幸至於大故，吾欲使子問於孟子，然後行事。」然友之鄒問於孟子。孟子曰：「不亦善乎！親喪固所自盡也。曾子曰：『生事之以禮；死葬之以禮，祭之以禮，可謂孝矣。』諸侯之禮，吾未之學也；雖然，吾嘗聞之矣。三年之喪，齊疏之服，飦粥之食，自天子達於庶人，三代共之。」
passages.translation_en: When Duke Ding of Teng died, the heir apparent said to Ran You, 'Once Mencius spoke with me in Song, and I have never been able to forget his words. Now that this great misfortune has befallen me, I wish to send you to consult Mencius before we proceed.' Ran You went to Zou and asked Mencius. Mencius said, 'Is this not excellent! In mourning for one's parents, one should certainly give it one's utmost. Zengzi said: "Serve them with propriety while they live; bury them with propriety when they die; sacrifice to them with propriety — this may be called filial." As for the rites of the feudal lords, I have not studied them; nevertheless, I have heard of them. The three-year mourning period, garments of coarse cloth with hemmed edges, and a diet of thin gruel — from the Son of Heaven down to the common people, this was the same across all three dynasties."

passages.text: 然友反命，定為三年之喪。父兄百官皆不欲，曰：「吾宗國魯先君莫之行，吾先君亦莫之行也，至於子之身而反之，不可。且志曰：『喪祭從先祖。』」曰：「吾有所受之也。」謂然友曰：「吾他日未嘗學問，好馳馬試劍。今也父兄百官不我足也，恐其不能盡於大事，子為我問孟子。」
passages.translation_en: Ran You returned and reported, and it was decided to observe the three-year mourning. The elder relatives and officials all opposed it, saying, 'The former rulers of Lu, our ancestral state, never practiced it, and our own former rulers never practiced it either. For you to reverse this in your own generation is unacceptable. Moreover, the records say: "In mourning and sacrifice, follow the ancestors."' The heir apparent said to Ran You, 'In the past I never applied myself to learning, preferring to gallop horses and fence with swords. Now the elder relatives and officials are not satisfied with me, and I fear I cannot do full justice to this great matter. Please consult Mencius on my behalf.'

passages.text: 然友復之鄒問孟子。孟子曰：「然。不可以他求者也。孔子曰：『君薨，聽於冢宰。歠粥，面深墨。即位而哭，百官有司，莫敢不哀，先之也。』上有好者，下必有甚焉者矣。『君子之德，風也；小人之德，草也。草尚之風必偃。』是在世子。」然友反命。世子曰：「然。是誠在我。」五月居廬，未有命戒。百官族人可謂曰知。及至葬，四方來觀之，顏色之戚，哭泣之哀，弔者大悅。
passages.translation_en: Ran You went again to Zou and asked Mencius. Mencius said, 'Yes. This is something where one cannot look to others. Confucius said: "When a ruler dies, authority is entrusted to the chief minister. The heir drinks thin gruel, and his face turns deeply dark. He takes his place and weeps, and none among the officials and functionaries dares not to grieve, because he has led by example." When those above have a preference, those below will surely carry it to excess. "The virtue of the gentleman is like the wind; the virtue of the common people is like the grass. When the wind blows over the grass, the grass must bend." This rests with the heir apparent.' Ran You returned and reported. The heir apparent said, 'Yes. This truly rests with me.' For five months he dwelt in the mourning hut, issuing no commands or instructions. The officials and kinsmen all acknowledged his wisdom. When the funeral came, people from all directions came to observe. The grief in his expression and the sorrow of his weeping greatly pleased those who came to offer condolences.

passages.text: 滕文公問為國。孟子曰：「民事不可緩也。《詩》云：『晝爾于茅，宵爾索綯；亟其乘屋，其始播百穀。』民之為道也，有恆產者有恆心，無恆產者無恆心。苟無恆心，放辟邪侈，無不為已。及陷乎罪，然後從而刑之，是罔民也。焉有仁人在位，罔民而可為也？是故賢君必恭儉禮下，取於民有制。陽虎曰：『為富不仁矣，為仁不富矣。』
passages.translation_en: Duke Wen of Teng asked about governing a state. Mencius said, 'The affairs of the people must not be delayed. The Odes say: "By day go gather thatch, by night twist it into rope; quickly repair the roof, for soon it will be time to sow the hundred grains." The way of the people is this: those with a steady livelihood have a steady heart; those without a steady livelihood lack a steady heart. And if they lack a steady heart, there is no dissipation, depravity, or excess they will not fall into. To wait until they have fallen into crime and then punish them — this is to entrap the people. How can a benevolent person in authority entrap the people and consider it acceptable? Therefore a worthy ruler must be respectful, frugal, and courteous to those below, and take from the people only according to regulation. Yang Hu said: "To pursue wealth is to be without benevolence; to pursue benevolence is to be without wealth."'

passages.text: 「夏后氏五十而貢，殷人七十而助，周人百畝而徹，其實皆什一也。徹者，徹也；助者，藉也。龍子曰：『治地莫善於助，莫不善於貢。貢者校數歲之中以為常。樂歲，粒米狼戾，多取之而不為虐，則寡取之；凶年，糞其田而不足，則必取盈焉。為民父母，使民盻盻然，將終歲勤動，不得以養其父母，又稱貸而益之。使老稚轉乎溝壑，惡在其為民父母也？』夫世祿，滕固行之矣。《詩》云：『雨我公田，遂及我私。』惟助為有公田。由此觀之，雖周亦助也。
passages.translation_en: 'Under the Xia dynasty, each family held fifty mu and paid tribute; under the Yin dynasty, each family held seventy mu under the aid system; under the Zhou dynasty, each family held a hundred mu under the tithe system. In reality, all amounted to a tax of one-tenth. The tithe means sharing; the aid system means lending labor. Long Zi said: "For land taxation, nothing is better than the aid system, and nothing worse than the tribute system. Under the tribute system, an average is calculated over several years to set a fixed amount. In good years, when grain is so abundant it goes to waste, one could take more without being oppressive, yet one takes only the fixed amount. In bad years, when the harvest does not even replenish the soil, one still demands the full amount. To act as parent of the people yet cause them to gaze about with resentful eyes — toiling all year long, unable to support their parents, forced to borrow at interest to make up the difference, so that the old and young end up dead in the ditches — where in this is being a parent to the people?" Now hereditary stipends are something Teng already practices. The Odes say: "May the rain fall on our public field and then extend to our private plots." Only the aid system has public fields. From this we can see that even under the Zhou, the aid system was used.'

passages.text: 「設為庠序學校以教之：庠者，養也；校者，教也；序者，射也。夏曰校，殷曰序，周曰庠，學則三代共之，皆所以明人倫也。人倫明於上，小民親於下。有王者起，必來取法，是為王者師也。《詩》云『周雖舊邦，其命惟新』，文王之謂也。子力行之，亦以新子之國。」
passages.translation_en: 'Establish xiang, xu, xue, and xiao schools to educate the people. Xiang means "to nourish"; xiao means "to teach"; xu means "archery" [and by extension, discipline]. The Xia dynasty called them xiao, the Yin called them xu, the Zhou called them xiang, while xue was the term shared by all three dynasties. The purpose of all of them was to illuminate the human relationships. When human relationships are made clear by those above, the common people below will be drawn together in affection. Should a true king arise, he would surely come to learn from you — you would be the teacher of a true king. The Odes say: "Although Zhou was an old state, its mandate was new" — this refers to King Wen. If you exert yourself in this, you too will make your state new.'

passages.text: 使畢戰問井地。孟子曰：「子之君將行仁政，選擇而使子，子必勉之！夫仁政，必自經界始。經界不正，井地不鈞，穀祿不平。是故暴君汙吏必慢其經界。經界既正，分田制祿可坐而定也。夫滕壤地褊小，將為君子焉，將為野人焉。無君子莫治野人，無野人莫養君子。請野九一而助，國中什一使自賦。卿以下必有圭田，圭田五十畝。餘夫二十五畝。死徙無出鄉，鄉田同井。出入相友，守望相助，疾病相扶持，則百姓親睦。方里而井，井九百畝，其中為公田。八家皆私百畝，同養公田。公事畢，然後敢治私事，所以別野人也。此其大略也。若夫潤澤之，則在君與子矣。」
passages.translation_en: The duke sent Bi Zhan to ask about the well-field system. Mencius said, 'Your ruler is about to practice benevolent government and has chosen you for the task — you must do your utmost! Benevolent government must begin with proper boundaries. If boundaries are not correct, the well-fields will be unequal and grain stipends will be unfair. Therefore tyrannical rulers and corrupt officials always neglect proper boundaries. Once boundaries are correctly set, the division of fields and regulation of stipends can be settled without difficulty. Now Teng is small in territory, but there will be gentlemen and there will be field workers. Without gentlemen, there is no one to govern the field workers; without field workers, there is no one to feed the gentlemen. In the countryside, let the tax be one-ninth under the aid system; in the capital, let it be one-tenth, self-assessed. From ministers on down, each must have a sacrificial field of fifty mu. Additional adult males receive twenty-five mu. Whether in death or removal, no one leaves their district. Those who share a well-field in their district go out and come in as companions, keep watch and help each other, and support one another in sickness — then the people will live in affection and harmony. A well-field is one li square, comprising nine hundred mu; the center is the public field. Eight families each hold a hundred mu privately and together cultivate the public field. Only after the public work is done may they attend to private affairs — this is what distinguishes the field workers. This is the general outline. As for refining and perfecting it, that rests with your ruler and with you.'

passages.text: 有為神農之言者許行，自楚之滕，踵門而告文公曰：「遠方之人聞君行仁政，願受一廛而為氓。」文公與之處，其徒數十人，皆衣褐，捆屨、織席以為食。陳良之徒陳相與其弟辛，負耒耜而自宋之滕，曰：「聞君行聖人之政，是亦聖人也，願為聖人氓。」陳相見許行而大悅，盡棄其學而學焉。陳相見孟子，道許行之言曰：「滕君，則誠賢君也；雖然，未聞道也。賢者與民並耕而食，饔飧而治。今也滕有倉廩府庫，則是厲民而以自養也，惡得賢？」
passages.translation_en: A man named Xu Xing, who professed the teachings of the Divine Farmer, came from Chu to Teng. He went to the gate and told Duke Wen, 'A man from afar has heard that you are practicing benevolent government, and wishes to receive a homestead and become your subject.' Duke Wen gave him a place to live. His followers, several dozen in number, all wore rough hemp, and they wove sandals and mats for their livelihood. Chen Xiang, a disciple of Chen Liang, and his brother Xin, carrying their plows on their backs, came from Song to Teng, saying, 'We have heard that you are practicing the government of a sage — you must be a sage yourself. We wish to become subjects of a sage.' Chen Xiang met Xu Xing and was greatly delighted; he abandoned all his former learning and became Xu Xing's student. Chen Xiang came to see Mencius and relayed Xu Xing's words: 'The ruler of Teng is truly a worthy ruler; nevertheless, he has not yet heard the Way. A worthy ruler should plow alongside his people and eat with them, preparing his own meals while governing. But now Teng has granaries and treasuries — this is to oppress the people in order to feed himself. How can he be called worthy?'

passages.text: 孟子曰：「許子必種粟而後食乎？」曰：「然。」「許子必織布而後衣乎？」曰：「否。許子衣褐。」「許子冠乎？」曰：「冠。」曰：「奚冠？」曰：「冠素。」曰：「自織之與？」曰：「否。以粟易之。」曰：「許子奚為不自織？」曰：「害於耕。」曰：「許子以釜甑爨，以鐵耕乎？」曰：「然。」「自為之與？」曰：「否。以粟易之。」
passages.translation_en: Mencius said, 'Does Master Xu eat only grain he has grown himself?' 'Yes.' 'Does Master Xu wear only cloth he has woven himself?' 'No. Master Xu wears rough hemp.' 'Does Master Xu wear a cap?' 'Yes.' 'What kind of cap?' 'A plain cap.' 'Does he weave it himself?' 'No. He trades grain for it.' 'Why does Master Xu not weave it himself?' 'It would interfere with his farming.' 'Does Master Xu cook with pots and pans and plow with iron?' 'Yes.' 'Does he make them himself?' 'No. He trades grain for them.'

passages.text: 「以粟易械器者，不為厲陶冶；陶冶亦以其械器易粟者，豈為厲農夫哉？且許子何不為陶冶。舍皆取諸其宮中而用之？何為紛紛然與百工交易？何許子之不憚煩？」曰：「百工之事，固不可耕且為也。」「然則治天下獨可耕且為與？有大人之事，有小人之事。且一人之身，而百工之所為備。如必自為而後用之，是率天下而路也。故曰：或勞心，或勞力；勞心者治人，勞力者治於人；治於人者食人，治人者食於人：天下之通義也。
passages.translation_en: 'When a farmer trades grain for pottery and tools, he does not thereby harm the potter or the smith; and when the potter and smith trade their wares for grain, they do not thereby harm the farmer. So why does Master Xu not become his own potter and smith, taking everything he needs from within his own household? Why does he bustle about trading with the hundred craftsmen? Why does Master Xu not shrink from the trouble?' Chen Xiang said, 'The work of the hundred crafts certainly cannot be carried on along with farming.' 'Then can governing the world alone be carried on along with farming? There are the affairs of great men, and there are the affairs of small men. Moreover, the products of all the hundred crafts are needed by every single person. If everyone had to make things for themselves before using them, this would lead the whole world to be constantly on the road. Therefore it is said: some labor with their minds, some labor with their strength. Those who labor with their minds govern others; those who labor with their strength are governed by others. Those who are governed feed others; those who govern are fed by others — this is a universal principle.'

passages.text: 「當堯之時，天下猶未平，洪水橫流，氾濫於天下。草木暢茂，禽獸繁殖，五穀不登，禽獸偪人。獸蹄鳥跡之道，交於中國。堯獨憂之，舉舜而敷治焉。舜使益掌火，益烈山澤而焚之，禽獸逃匿。禹疏九河，瀹濟漯，而注諸海；決汝漢，排淮泗，而注之江，然後中國可得而食也。當是時也，禹八年於外，三過其門而不入，雖欲耕，得乎？后稷教民稼穡。樹藝五穀，五穀熟而民人育。人之有道也，飽食、煖衣、逸居而無教，則近於禽獸。聖人有憂之，使契為司徒，教以人倫：父子有親，君臣有義，夫婦有別，長幼有序，朋友有信。放勳曰：『勞之來之，匡之直之，輔之翼之，使自得之，又從而振德之。』聖人之憂民如此，而暇耕乎？
passages.translation_en: 'In the time of Yao, the world was not yet settled. Floodwaters flowed recklessly, inundating the land. Plants and trees grew in wild profusion, birds and beasts multiplied, the five grains did not ripen, and the birds and beasts encroached upon the people. Trails of animal hooves and bird tracks crisscrossed the Central States. Yao alone was troubled by this and raised up Shun to bring order. Shun appointed Yi to take charge of fire; Yi set fire to the mountains and marshes, and the birds and beasts fled into hiding. Yu channeled the nine rivers, cleared the courses of the Ji and the Ta, and directed them to the sea; he opened the Ru and the Han, cleared the Huai and the Si, and directed them into the Yangtze — only then could the Central States be farmed and fed. During that time, Yu spent eight years abroad and passed his own door three times without entering. Even had he wished to farm, could he have? Hou Ji taught the people to plant and harvest; they cultivated the five grains, and when the grains ripened, the people were nourished. But human beings have a Way: if they are well-fed, warmly clothed, and live at ease but receive no education, they come close to being animals. The sages were troubled by this and appointed Xie as Minister of Education to teach the people human relationships: affection between parent and child, righteousness between ruler and minister, distinct roles between husband and wife, proper order between elder and younger, and trust between friends. Yao said: "Encourage them, guide them, correct them, straighten them, help them, support them, enable them to find it in themselves, and then further uplift their virtue." The sages' concern for the people was like this — could they have had time to farm?'

passages.text: 「堯以不得舜為己憂，舜以不得禹、皋陶為己憂。夫以百畝之不易為己憂者，農夫也。分人以財謂之惠，教人以善謂之忠，為天下得人者謂之仁。是故以天下與人易，為天下得人難。孔子曰：『大哉堯之為君！惟天為大，惟堯則之，蕩蕩乎民無能名焉！君哉舜也！巍巍乎有天下而不與焉！』堯舜之治天下，豈無所用其心哉？亦不用於耕耳。
passages.translation_en: 'Yao regarded not finding Shun as his own greatest worry; Shun regarded not finding Yu and Gao Yao as his own greatest worry. One who worries about his hundred mu not being properly tilled is a farmer. To share one's wealth with others is called generosity; to teach others to be good is called loyalty; to find the right person for the world is called benevolence. Thus it is easy to give the world to someone, but hard to find the right person for the world. Confucius said: "How great was Yao as a ruler! Only Heaven is great, and only Yao measured up to it. So vast was his virtue that the people could find no name for it! What a ruler Shun was! How lofty — he possessed the world and yet took no personal part in it!" Did Yao and Shun govern the world without using their minds? They simply did not use them on farming.'

passages.text: 「吾聞用夏變夷者，未聞變於夷者也。陳良，楚產也。悅周公、仲尼之道，北學於中國。北方之學者，未能或之先也。彼所謂豪傑之士也。子之兄弟事之數十年，師死而遂倍之。昔者孔子沒，三年之外，門人治任將歸，入揖於子貢，相向而哭，皆失聲，然後歸。子貢反，築室於場，獨居三年，然後歸。他日，子夏、子張、子游以有若似聖人，欲以所事孔子事之，彊曾子。曾子曰：『不可。江漢以濯之，秋陽以暴之，皜皜乎不可尚已。』今也南蠻鴃舌之人，非先王之道，子倍子之師而學之，亦異於曾子矣。吾聞出於幽谷遷于喬木者，末聞下喬木而入於幽谷者。《魯頌》曰：『戎狄是膺，荊舒是懲。』周公方且膺之，子是之學，亦為不善變矣。」
passages.translation_en: 'I have heard of using the ways of the Central States to transform barbarians, but I have never heard of being transformed by barbarians. Chen Liang was a native of Chu. Delighting in the Way of the Duke of Zhou and Confucius, he traveled north to study in the Central States. Among the scholars of the north, none had been able to surpass him. He was what one would call a truly outstanding man. You and your brother studied under him for decades, and when your teacher died you turned your back on him. In the past, when Confucius died, after three years his disciples packed their bags to go home. Before leaving, they went in to bow to Zigong, and facing one another they wept until they lost their voices, and only then departed. Zigong went back and built a hut by the burial ground, where he lived alone for three more years before going home. On another occasion, Zixia, Zizhang, and Ziyou, thinking that You Ruo resembled the sage, wished to serve him as they had served Confucius, and tried to compel Zengzi to join them. Zengzi said: "That must not be. Washed by the waters of the Yangtze and the Han, bleached by the autumn sun — so dazzling white that nothing can surpass it." Now here is a man of the southern barbarians with a twittering tongue who denounces the Way of the ancient kings, and you turn your back on your teacher to study under him — you are quite different from Zengzi. I have heard of birds leaving dark valleys to move to tall trees, but I have never heard of them descending from tall trees into dark valleys. The Lu Hymns say: "Strike the Rong and Di, punish Jing and Shu." The Duke of Zhou was about to strike them — yet you choose to learn from them. This is hardly a change for the better.'

passages.text: 「從許子之道，則市賈不貳，國中無偽。雖使五尺之童適市，莫之或欺。布帛長短同，則賈相若；麻縷絲絮輕重同，則賈相若；五穀多寡同，則賈相若；屨大小同，則賈相若。」曰：「夫物之不齊，物之情也；或相倍蓰，或相什伯，或相千萬。子比而同之，是亂天下也。巨屨小屨同賈，人豈為之哉？從許子之道，相率而為偽者也，惡能治國家？」墨者夷之，因徐辟而求見孟子。孟子曰：「吾固願見，今吾尚病，病愈，我且往見，夷子不來！」
passages.translation_en: 'If we follow Master Xu's way, then market prices will not vary and there will be no deception in the state. Even if you send a small child to the market, no one will cheat him. Cloth of the same length will sell at the same price; hemp, silk, and cotton of the same weight will sell at the same price; grain of the same quantity will sell at the same price; shoes of the same size will sell at the same price.' Mencius said, 'That things are unequal is the nature of things. Some differ by twice or five times, some by ten or a hundred times, some by a thousand or ten thousand times. If you try to level them all, you will throw the world into chaos. If fine shoes and coarse shoes are priced the same, who would make fine shoes? To follow Master Xu's way would be to lead everyone into deception — how could that govern a state?' A Mohist named Yi Zhi sought through Xu Bi to see Mencius. Mencius said, 'I would certainly like to see him, but I am still ill. When I have recovered, I will go to see him. Yi Zhi need not come.'

passages.text: 他日又求見孟子。孟子曰：「吾今則可以見矣。不直，則道不見；我且直之。吾聞夷子墨者。墨之治喪也，以薄為其道也。夷子思以易天下，豈以為非是而不貴也？然而夷子葬其親厚，則是以所賤事親也。」徐子以告夷子。夷子曰：「儒者之道，古之人『若保赤子』，此言何謂也？之則以為愛無差等，施由親始。」
passages.translation_en: Another day, Yi Zhi again sought to see Mencius. Mencius said, 'Now I can see him. If I am not straightforward, the Way will not be made clear, so let me be direct. I have heard that Yi Zhi is a Mohist. In Mohist funeral practice, frugality is taken as the guiding principle. Yi Zhi intends to change the world with this — surely he considers lavish funerals wrong and unworthy. And yet Yi Zhi buried his own parents lavishly. This means he treated his parents with what he himself considers base.' Xu Bi reported this to Yi Zhi. Yi Zhi said, 'According to the Confucian Way, the ancients "cared for the people as if caring for a newborn" — what does this mean? I take it to mean that love knows no gradations, but its practice begins with one's parents.'

passages.text: 徐子以告孟子。孟子曰：「夫夷子，信以為人之親其兄之子為若親其鄰之赤子乎？彼有取爾也。赤子匍匐將入井，非赤子之罪也。且天之生物也，使之一本，而夷子二本故也。蓋上世嘗有不葬其親者。其親死，則舉而委之於壑。他日過之，狐狸食之，蠅蚋姑嘬之。其顙有泚，睨而不視。夫泚也，非為人泚，中心達於面目。蓋歸反虆梩而掩之。掩之誠是也，則孝子仁人之掩其親，亦必有道矣。」徐子以告夷子。夷子憮然為閒曰：「命之矣。」
passages.translation_en: Xu Bi reported this to Mencius. Mencius said, 'Does Yi Zhi truly believe that a person's love for his brother's child is the same as his love for a neighbor's infant? The passage he cited has a specific point: when an infant crawls toward a well, it is not the infant's fault — this is what it means. Moreover, Heaven produces living things from a single root, but Yi Zhi would give them two roots. Presumably in ancient times there were those who did not bury their parents. When their parents died, they picked up the bodies and threw them into a ditch. Later, passing by, they saw foxes and wild cats gnawing at them and flies and gnats swarming over them. Sweat broke out on their foreheads; they looked away and could not bear to look. That sweating was not for the sake of others — it was a feeling from the innermost heart breaking through to the face. They went home, returned with baskets and shovels, and covered the bodies. If covering them was truly right, then filial children and benevolent people who cover their parents must also have a proper Way of doing so.' Xu Bi reported this to Yi Zhi. Yi Zhi stood in a daze for a moment and said, 'He has taught me.'

passages.text: 陳代曰：「不見諸侯，宜若小然；今一見之，大則以王，小則以霸。且志曰：『枉尺而直尋』，宜若可為也。」
passages.translation_en: Chen Dai said: "Not going to see the feudal lords seems like a small thing to insist on. Yet if you were to see them just once, at best you could help them become a true king, and at least help them become a hegemon. Moreover, the records say: 'Bend one foot to straighten eight feet' — that seems worth doing."

passages.text: 孟子曰：「昔齊景公田，招虞人以旌，不至，將殺之。志士不忘在溝壑，勇士不忘喪其元。孔子奚取焉？取非其招不往也，如不待其招而往，何哉？且夫枉尺而直尋者，以利言也。如以利，則枉尋直尺而利，亦可為與？昔者趙簡子使王良與嬖奚乘，終日而不獲一禽。嬖奚反命曰：『天下之賤工也。』或以告王良。良曰：『請復之。』彊而後可，一朝而獲十禽。嬖奚反命曰：『天下之良工也。』簡子曰：『我使掌與女乘。』謂王良。良不可，曰：『吾為之範我馳驅，終日不獲一；為之詭遇，一朝而獲十。《詩》云：「不失其馳，舍矢如破。」我不貫與小人乘，請辭。』御者且羞與射者比。比而得禽獸，雖若丘陵，弗為也。如枉道而從彼，何也？且子過矣，枉己者，未有能直人者也。」
passages.translation_en: Mencius said: "In the past, Duke Jing of Qi went hunting and summoned his gamekeeper with a pennant. The gamekeeper would not come, and the duke was about to have him killed. 'A man of resolve never forgets he may end up in a ditch; a brave man never forgets he may lose his head.' What did Confucius admire in this? He admired that the man would not go when summoned improperly. What would it mean to go without even waiting for a proper summons? Furthermore, this talk of 'bending one foot to straighten eight feet' is reasoning based on profit. If we follow profit, then bending eight feet to straighten one foot would also be acceptable, so long as it were profitable — would you do that too? In the past, Zhao Jianzi had Wang Liang drive a chariot for his favorite, Xi. They went out for a whole day without catching a single bird. Xi reported back: 'He is the worst driver in the world.' Someone told Wang Liang about this. Liang said: 'Let me try again.' He insisted, and Xi reluctantly agreed. In a single morning they caught ten birds. Xi reported back: 'He is the best driver in the world.' Jianzi said: 'I will assign him to drive for you regularly.' He told Wang Liang, but Liang refused, saying: 'When I drove properly for him, we went a whole day without catching anything. When I used irregular methods, we caught ten in a single morning. The Odes say: "He does not miss his course; his arrows fly as if to shatter the target." I am not accustomed to driving for petty men — please let me decline.' Even a chariot driver would be ashamed to conspire with a hunter. If by conspiring one could pile up game like hills, a true driver still would not do it. If you bend the Way to follow such people, what is the point? Besides, you are wrong: no one who bends himself has ever been able to straighten others."

passages.text: 景春曰：「公孫衍、張儀豈不誠大丈夫哉？一怒而諸侯懼，安居而天下熄。」孟子曰：「是焉得為大丈夫乎？子未學禮乎？丈夫之冠也，父命之；女子之嫁也，母命之，往送之門，戒之曰：『往之女家，必敬必戒，無違夫子！』以順為正者，妾婦之道也。居天下之廣居，立天下之正位，行天下之大道。得志與民由之，不得志獨行其道。富貴不能淫，貧賤不能移，威武不能屈。此之謂大丈夫。」周霄問曰：「古之君子仕乎？」
passages.translation_en: Jing Chun said: "Are not Gongsun Yan and Zhang Yi truly great men? When they are angry, the feudal lords tremble; when they are at ease, the world is at peace." Mencius said: "How can they be considered great men? Have you not studied the rites? When a young man is capped, his father instructs him; when a young woman is married, her mother instructs her. Seeing her off at the gate, the mother warns: 'When you go to your husband's house, you must be respectful and careful — never disobey your husband!' To take obedience as the standard — that is the way of a concubine. A true great man dwells in the broad house of the world — benevolence; stands in the correct position of the world — propriety; walks the great road of the world — righteousness. When he achieves his ambitions, he shares the Way with the people; when he does not, he walks the Way alone. Wealth and rank cannot corrupt him, poverty and low station cannot sway him, power and force cannot bend him. This is what I call a great man." Zhou Xiao asked: "Did the gentlemen of antiquity serve in government?"

passages.text: 孟子曰：「仕。傳曰：『孔子三月無君，則皇皇如也，出疆必載質。』公明儀曰：『古之人三月無君則弔。』」「三月無君則弔，不以急乎？」曰：「士之失位也，猶諸侯之失國家也。禮曰：『諸侯耕助，以供粢盛；夫人蠶繅，以為衣服。犧牲不成，粢盛不潔，衣服不備，不敢以祭。惟士無田，則亦不祭。』牲殺器皿衣服不備，不敢以祭，則不敢以宴，亦不足弔乎？」「出疆必載質，何也？」
passages.translation_en: Mencius said: "They did. The records say: 'When Confucius went three months without a ruler to serve, he became anxious and uneasy; when he left a state, he always carried his ceremonial gifts with him.' Gongming Yi said: 'Among the ancients, if one went three months without a ruler, friends would come to offer condolences.'" "If three months without a ruler calls for condolences, is that not overly urgent?" Mencius said: "A scholar losing his position is like a feudal lord losing his state. The Rites say: 'The feudal lords plow the communal fields to supply the sacrificial grain; their consorts tend silkworms and reel silk to make the sacrificial garments. If the sacrificial animals are not fit, the grain is not pure, and the garments are not prepared, they dare not sacrifice. Likewise, if a scholar has no land, he too cannot sacrifice.' If the animals, vessels, and garments are not prepared so that one dares not sacrifice, then one dares not feast either — is that not also worthy of condolences?" "Why did Confucius always carry ceremonial gifts when leaving a state?"

passages.text: 曰：「士之仕也，猶農夫之耕也，農夫豈為出疆舍其耒耜哉？」曰：「晉國亦仕國也，未嘗聞仕如此其急。仕如此其急也，君子之難仕，何也？」曰：「丈夫生而願為之有室，女子生而願為之有家。父母之心，人皆有之。不待父母之命、媒妁之言，鑽穴隙相窺，踰牆相從，則父母國人皆賤之。古之人未嘗不欲仕也，又惡不由其道。不由其道而往者，與鑽穴隙之類也。」彭更問曰：「後車數十乘，從者數百人，以傳食於諸侯，不以泰乎？」
passages.translation_en: Mencius said: "A scholar's service in government is like a farmer's plowing — would a farmer abandon his plow and hoe just because he crosses a border?" Zhou Xiao said: "The state of Jin also employs officials, yet I have never heard of such urgency about office. If seeking office is this urgent, why is it that a gentleman finds it difficult to take office?" Mencius said: "When a boy is born, his parents wish for him to have a wife; when a girl is born, they wish for her to have a husband. All parents share this feeling. But if the young, without waiting for their parents' permission or a matchmaker's introduction, bore holes through walls to peek at each other and climb over fences to be together, then parents and countrymen alike would despise them. The ancients certainly desired to serve in government, but they also hated to do so by improper means. To seek office through improper means is of the same kind as boring through walls." Peng Geng asked: "Is it not excessive to travel with dozens of carriages and hundreds of followers, eating your way from one feudal lord to another?"

passages.text: 孟子曰：「非其道，則一簞食不可受於人；如其道，則舜受堯之天下，不以為泰，子以為泰乎？」曰：「否。士無事而食，不可也。」曰：「子不通功易事，以羡補不足，則農有餘粟，女有餘布；子如通之，則梓匠輪輿皆得食於子。於此有人焉，入則孝，出則悌，守先王之道，以待後之學者，而不得食於子。子何尊梓匠輪輿而輕為仁義者哉？」曰：「梓匠輪輿，其志將以求食也；君子之為道也，其志亦將以求食與？」
passages.translation_en: Mencius said: "If it is not in accordance with the Way, then one should not accept even a single basket of rice from another person. But if it is in accordance with the Way, then Shun accepted the whole empire from Yao without considering it excessive — would you consider it excessive?" Peng Geng said: "No. But it is wrong for a scholar to eat without working." Mencius said: "If you do not allow the exchange of goods and services so that surpluses make up for deficits, then farmers will have excess grain and weavers will have excess cloth. But if you do allow such exchange, then carpenters, wheelwrights, and carriage-makers can all get food from you. Now suppose there is a person who is filial at home, respectful abroad, who guards the Way of the ancient kings to pass it on to future learners — and yet he cannot get food from you. Why do you honor carpenters and wheelwrights but look down on those who practice benevolence and righteousness?" Peng Geng said: "The carpenters and wheelwrights have the intention of seeking food by their work. When a gentleman pursues the Way, is his intention also to seek food?"

passages.text: 曰：「子何以其志為哉？其有功於子，可食而食之矣。且子食志乎？食功乎？」曰：「食志。」曰：「有人於此，毀瓦畫墁，其志將以求食也，則子食之乎？」曰：「否。」曰：「然則子非食志也，食功也。」萬章問曰：「宋，小國也。今將行王政，齊楚惡而伐之，則如之何？」
passages.translation_en: Mencius said: "Why must you judge by intentions? If someone renders you a service, you may feed him and that is that. Besides, do you feed people based on their intentions, or on their actual contributions?" Peng Geng said: "Their intentions." Mencius said: "Suppose someone here smashes your tiles and scrawls over your freshly plastered walls, and his intention is to earn food by it — would you feed him?" Peng Geng said: "No." Mencius said: "Then you do not feed based on intentions after all — you feed based on actual contributions." Wan Zhang asked: "Song is a small state. Now if it tries to implement true kingly government and Qi and Chu become hostile and attack it, what should be done?"

passages.text: 孟子曰：「湯居亳，與葛為鄰，葛伯放而不祀。湯使人問之曰：『何為不祀？』曰：『無以供犧牲也。』湯使遺之牛羊。葛伯食之，又不以祀。湯又使人問之曰：『何為不祀？』曰：『無以供粢盛也。』湯使亳眾往為之耕，老弱饋食。葛伯率其民，要其有酒食黍稻者奪之，不授者殺之。有童子以黍肉餉，殺而奪之。《書》曰：『葛伯仇餉。』此之謂也。為其殺是童子而征之，四海之內皆曰：『非富天下也，為匹夫匹婦復讎也。』『湯始征，自葛載』，十一征而無敵於天下。東面而征，西夷怨；南面而征，北狄怨，曰：『奚為後我？』民之望之，若大旱之望雨也。歸市者弗止，芸者不變，誅其君，弔其民，如時雨降。民大悅。《書》曰：『徯我后，后來其無罰。』『有攸不惟臣，東征，綏厥士女，匪厥玄黃，紹我周王見休，惟臣附于大邑周。』其君子實玄黃于匪以迎其君子，其小人簞食壺漿以迎其小人，救民於水火之中，取其殘而已矣。《太誓》曰：『我武惟揚，侵于之疆，則取于殘，殺伐用張，于湯有光。』不行王政云爾，苟行王政，四海之內皆舉首而望之，欲以為君。齊楚雖大，何畏焉？」
passages.translation_en: Mencius said: "When Tang dwelt in Bo, he was neighbor to the lord of Ge. The lord of Ge was dissolute and did not sacrifice. Tang sent someone to ask: 'Why do you not sacrifice?' He replied: 'I have no animals for the offerings.' Tang sent him oxen and sheep. The lord of Ge ate them but still did not sacrifice. Tang again sent someone to ask why. He replied: 'I have no grain for the offerings.' Tang sent the people of Bo to plow his fields for him, and the old and weak brought them food. But the lord of Ge led his people to waylay those who brought wine, food, millet, and rice, and robbed them — killing those who would not hand them over. A boy bringing millet and meat was killed and robbed. The Book of Documents says: 'The lord of Ge treated the food-bringers as enemies.' This is what it refers to. Tang punished him for killing that boy, and all within the four seas said: 'He is not seeking to enrich himself with the empire — he is avenging ordinary men and women.' 'Tang's campaigns began with Ge.' In eleven campaigns he had no rival in the empire. When he marched east, the western tribes complained; when he marched south, the northern tribes complained, saying: 'Why does he leave us for last?' The people longed for him as people in a great drought long for rain. Those going to market were not stopped, and those weeding their fields went on as before. He punished the rulers but comforted the people, like timely rain falling. The people were overjoyed. The Book of Documents says: 'We have waited for our lord; when our lord comes, we shall suffer no more.' 'There were those who would not submit. He campaigned east, bringing peace to the men and women there. They came bearing baskets of dark silk and yellow silk to welcome him, saying: "Welcome our lord of Zhou, that we may receive his blessings and become subjects of the great city of Zhou."' Their gentlemen came with baskets of silk to welcome his gentlemen; their common people came with baskets of food and jugs of drink to welcome his common people. He saved the people from fire and flood, seizing only the tyrants. The Great Declaration says: 'Our martial power is displayed; we invade his territory, seize the tyrants, and our punitive glory shines — more glorious even than Tang.' If one does not practice kingly government, so be it. But if one does, all within the four seas will raise their heads in hope, wishing to make him their ruler. Though Qi and Chu are great, what is there to fear?"

passages.text: 孟子謂戴不勝曰：「子欲子之王之善與？我明告子。有楚大夫於此，欲其子之齊語也，則使齊人傅諸？使楚人傅諸？」曰：「使齊人傅之。」曰：「一齊人傅之，眾楚人咻之，雖日撻而求其齊也，不可得矣；引而置之莊嶽之間數年，雖日撻而求其楚，亦不可得矣。子謂薛居州，善士也。使之居於王所。在於王所者，長幼卑尊，皆薛居州也，王誰與為不善？在王所者，長幼卑尊，皆非薛居州也，王誰與為善？一薛居州，獨如宋王何？」
passages.translation_en: Mencius said to Dai Busheng: "You want your king to become good? Let me explain it plainly. Suppose a Chu nobleman here wants his son to speak the language of Qi — would he have a man of Qi tutor the boy, or a man of Chu?" "A man of Qi," Dai answered. Mencius said: "If one man of Qi tutors him while a crowd of Chu men jabber around him, even if you beat the boy daily demanding he speak Qi dialect, it will be impossible. But if you took him and placed him in the Zhuang-Yue district of Qi for several years, even if you beat him daily demanding he speak Chu dialect, that too would be impossible. You say Xue Juzhou is a good man and have placed him at court. But if everyone at court, old and young, high and low, were a Xue Juzhou, then with whom would the king do wrong? And if no one at court, old or young, high or low, is a Xue Juzhou, then with whom would the king do right? What can a single Xue Juzhou do about the king of Song?"

passages.text: 公孫丑問曰：「不見諸侯何義？」孟子曰：「古者不為臣不見。段干木踰垣而辟之，泄柳閉門而不內，是皆已甚。迫，斯可以見矣。陽貨欲見孔子而惡無禮，大夫有賜於士，不得受於其家，則往拜其門。陽貨矙孔子之亡也，而饋孔子蒸豚；孔子亦矙其亡也，而往拜之。當是時，陽貨先，豈得不見？曾子曰：『脅肩諂笑，病于夏畦。』子路曰：『未同而言，觀其色赧赧然，非由之所知也。』由是觀之，則君子之所養可知已矣。」
passages.translation_en: Gongsun Chou asked: "What is the principle behind not going to see feudal lords?" Mencius said: "In antiquity, if one was not a minister, one did not seek an audience. Duan Ganmu leapt over a wall to avoid a lord's visit; Xie Liu shut his gate and refused entry. These were excessive. If one is pressed, then one may agree to meet. Yang Huo wanted to see Confucius but disliked appearing discourteous. The rule was that if a great officer sent a gift to a scholar who was not home to receive it, the scholar must go to the officer's gate to pay respects. Yang Huo watched for a time when Confucius was out and sent him a steamed piglet. Confucius likewise watched for a time when Yang Huo was out and went to pay his respects. At that point, Yang Huo had made the first move — how could Confucius have refused to see him? Zengzi said: 'Hunching your shoulders and forcing a flattering smile is more exhausting than working in a summer garden.' Zilu said: 'To speak with someone you are not in accord with, and watch his face flush with shame — that is beyond my understanding.' From this we can see what the gentleman values in self-cultivation."

passages.text: 戴盈之曰：「什一，去關市之征，今茲未能。請輕之，以待來年，然後已，何如？」孟子曰：「今有人日攘其鄰之雞者，或告之曰：『是非君子之道。』曰：『請損之，月攘一雞，以待來年，然後已。』如知其非義，斯速已矣，何待來年。」公都子曰：「外人皆稱夫子好辯，敢問何也？」
passages.translation_en: Dai Yingzhi said: "A tax of one in ten, and the abolition of tariffs and market taxes — I cannot manage it this year. May I reduce them gradually, and wait until next year to complete it? What do you think?" Mencius said: "Suppose there is a man who steals one of his neighbor's chickens every day. Someone tells him: 'This is not the way of a gentleman.' He replies: 'Let me reduce it — I will steal one chicken a month, and wait until next year to stop completely.' If you know something is wrong, you should stop it at once. Why wait until next year?" Gongduzi said: "Outsiders all say that you, Master, are fond of disputation. May I ask why?"

passages.text: 孟子曰：「予豈好辯哉？予不得已也。天下之生久矣，一治一亂。當堯之時，水逆行，氾濫於中國。蛇龍居之，民無所定。下者為巢，上者為營窟。《書》曰：『洚水警余。』洚水者，洪水也。使禹治之，禹掘地而注之海，驅蛇龍而放之菹。水由地中行，江、淮、河、漢是也。險阻既遠，鳥獸之害人者消，然後人得平土而居之。
passages.translation_en: Mencius said: "How could I be fond of disputation? I have no choice. The world has existed for a long time, alternating between order and chaos. In the time of Yao, the waters flowed backward and flooded the Central Kingdom. Snakes and dragons made their homes there, and the people had nowhere to settle. Those on low ground built nests in trees; those on high ground dug burrows in the hillsides. The Book of Documents says: 'The floodwaters warn me.' The floodwaters were the great flood. Yu was sent to control them. He dug channels to drain the water into the sea and drove the snakes and dragons into the marshes. The water flowed through the channels in the earth — the Yangtze, the Huai, the Yellow River, and the Han. Once the dangers were removed and the birds and beasts that had plagued the people were gone, people were at last able to live on level ground.

passages.text: 「堯、舜既沒，聖人之道衰。暴君代作，壞宮室以為汙池，民無所安息；棄田以為園囿，使民不得衣食。邪說暴行又作，園囿、汙池、沛澤多而禽獸至。及紂之身，天下又大亂。周公相武王，誅紂伐奄，三年討其君，驅飛廉於海隅而戮之。滅國者五十，驅虎、豹、犀、象而遠之。天下大悅。《書》曰：『丕顯哉，文王謨！丕承哉，武王烈！佑啟我後人，咸以正無缺。』
passages.translation_en: "After Yao and Shun passed away, the Way of the sages declined. Tyrants arose one after another, tearing down homes to make pleasure ponds so the people had no rest, and abandoning farmland to make parks and gardens so the people could not feed and clothe themselves. Heresies and violence flourished again; as parks, ponds, and marshes multiplied, wild beasts appeared everywhere. By the time of Zhou, the world was again in great chaos. The Duke of Zhou assisted King Wu, punished Zhou the tyrant and conquered Yan; after three years he brought their rulers to justice. He drove Fei Lian to a corner of the sea and executed him. He destroyed fifty states and drove tigers, leopards, rhinoceroses, and elephants far away. The whole world rejoiced. The Book of Documents says: 'How brilliant were the plans of King Wen! How great were the achievements of King Wu! They aid and enlighten us who come after, so that all is correct and without flaw.'

passages.text: 「世衰道微，邪說暴行有作，臣弒其君者有之，子弒其父者有之。孔子懼，作《春秋》。《春秋》，天子之事也。是故孔子曰：『知我者其惟春秋乎！罪我者其惟春秋乎！』
passages.translation_en: "As the age declined and the Way grew faint, heresies and violence arose. There were ministers who murdered their rulers and sons who murdered their fathers. Confucius was alarmed and composed the Spring and Autumn Annals. The Spring and Autumn Annals deals with matters that belong to the Son of Heaven. Therefore Confucius said: 'Those who understand me will do so through the Spring and Autumn Annals; those who condemn me will do so through the Spring and Autumn Annals.'

passages.text: 「聖王不作，諸侯放恣，處士橫議，楊朱、墨翟之言盈天下。天下之言，不歸楊，則歸墨。楊氏為我，是無君也；墨氏兼愛，是無父也。無父無君，是禽獸也。公明儀曰：『庖有肥肉，廄有肥馬，民有飢色，野有餓莩，此率獸而食人也。』楊墨之道不息，孔子之道不著，是邪說誣民，充塞仁義也。仁義充塞，則率獸食人，人將相食。吾為此懼，閑先聖之道，距楊墨，放淫辭，邪說者不得作。作於其心，害於其事；作於其事，害於其政。聖人復起，不易吾言矣。
passages.translation_en: "No sage king has arisen. The feudal lords are dissolute and willful. Unemployed scholars engage in reckless argument. The words of Yang Zhu and Mo Di fill the world. The teachings of the world, if not following Yang, follow Mo. Yang's doctrine of 'for oneself' denies the ruler; Mo's doctrine of 'universal love' denies the father. To deny father and ruler is to be no better than the beasts. Gongming Yi said: 'In the kitchen there is fat meat; in the stable there are fat horses; yet the people have the look of hunger, and in the wilds there are those who have starved to death — this is leading beasts to devour men.' If the Way of Yang and Mo does not cease and the Way of Confucius is not made manifest, then these heresies will deceive the people and block up benevolence and righteousness. When benevolence and righteousness are blocked, beasts are led to devour men, and men will devour one another. I am alarmed by this. I defend the Way of the ancient sages, oppose Yang and Mo, and banish their licentious words, so that the authors of heresies cannot prevail. When heresy arises in the mind, it harms one's conduct; when it arises in one's conduct, it harms one's governance. Should a sage arise again, he would not change my words.

passages.text: 「昔者禹抑洪水而天下平，周公兼夷狄驅猛獸而百姓寧，孔子成《春秋》而亂臣賊子懼。《詩》云：『戎狄是膺，荊舒是懲，則莫我敢承。』無父無君，是周公所膺也。我亦欲正人心，息邪說，距詖行，放淫辭，以承三聖者；豈好辯哉？予不得已也。能言距楊墨者，聖人之徒也。」匡章曰：「陳仲子豈不誠廉士哉？居於陵，三日不食，耳無聞，目無見也。井上有李，螬食實者過半矣，匍匐往將食之，三咽，然後耳有聞，目有見。」
passages.translation_en: "In the past, Yu suppressed the floodwaters and the world was at peace. The Duke of Zhou subjugated the barbarians and drove away the fierce beasts, and the people found tranquility. Confucius completed the Spring and Autumn Annals, and rebellious ministers and unfilial sons were struck with fear. The Odes say: 'He struck the Rong and Di, he punished Jing and Shu, and none dared stand against us.' Those who deny father and ruler — they are the ones the Duke of Zhou struck down. I too wish to rectify people's hearts, put an end to heresies, oppose crooked conduct, and banish licentious words, in order to carry on the work of these three sages. How could I be fond of disputation? I have no choice. Whoever can argue against Yang and Mo is a disciple of the sages." Kuang Zhang said: "Is Chen Zhongzi not truly a man of integrity? Living in Yuling, he went three days without eating — his ears could not hear, his eyes could not see. Above a well there was a plum tree, its fruit more than half eaten by worms. He crawled over, took it, and ate it. After three bites, his ears could hear and his eyes could see again."

passages.text: 孟子曰：「於齊國之士，吾必以仲子為巨擘焉。雖然，仲子惡能廉？充仲子之操，則蚓而後可者也。夫蚓，上食槁壤，下飲黃泉。仲子所居之室，伯夷之所築與？抑亦盜跖之所築與？所食之粟，伯夷之所樹與？抑亦盜跖之所樹與？是未可知也。」曰：「是何傷哉？彼身織屨，妻辟纑，以易之也。」
passages.translation_en: Mencius said: "Among the scholars of Qi, I would certainly regard Zhongzi as the foremost. Nevertheless, how can Zhongzi truly be called a man of integrity? To fully carry out Zhongzi's principles, one would have to be an earthworm to succeed. An earthworm eats dry earth above and drinks from the yellow springs below. But the house Zhongzi lives in — was it built by a Bo Yi, or by a Robber Zhi? The grain he eats — was it planted by a Bo Yi, or by a Robber Zhi? This we cannot know." Kuang Zhang said: "What does that matter? He weaves sandals himself and his wife spins hemp thread, and they trade these for what they need."

passages.text: 曰：「仲子，齊之世家也。兄戴，蓋祿萬鍾。以兄之祿為不義之祿而不食也，以兄之室為不義之室而不居也，辟兄離母，處於於陵。他日歸，則有饋其兄生鵝者，己頻顣曰：『惡用是鶃鶃者為哉？』他日，其母殺是鵝也，與之食之。其兄自外至，曰：『是鶃鶃之肉也。』出而哇之。以母則不食，以妻則食之；以兄之室則弗居，以於陵則居之。是尚為能充其類也乎？若仲子者，蚓而後充其操者也。」
passages.translation_en: Mencius said: "Zhongzi belongs to one of Qi's most prominent families. His elder brother Dai received an emolument of ten thousand zhong from the fief of Gai. Zhongzi regarded his brother's emolument as unrighteous and would not eat from it; he regarded his brother's house as unrighteous and would not live in it. He left his brother and mother and went to live in Yuling. One day he returned home and found that someone had given his brother a live goose. He knit his brows and said: 'What use is this honking thing?' Another day, his mother killed the goose and served it to him, and he ate it. His brother came in from outside and said: 'That is the meat of that honking thing.' Zhongzi went out and vomited it up. He will not eat what his mother provides, but he eats what his wife provides; he will not live in his brother's house, but he lives in Yuling. Can this be considered fully carrying out his principles? Someone like Zhongzi — only by becoming an earthworm could he truly fulfill his standards."

passages.text: 孟子曰：「離婁之明，公輸子之巧，不以規矩，不能成方員：師曠之聰，不以六律，不能正五音；堯舜之道，不以仁政，不能平治天下。今有仁心仁聞而民不被其澤，不可法於後世者，不行先王之道也。
passages.translation_en: Mencius said: "Even with the sharp eyes of Li Lou and the skill of Gongshu Ban, without compass and square one cannot make perfect circles and squares. Even with the keen ears of Music Master Kuang, without the six pitch-pipes one cannot tune the five notes correctly. Even with the Way of Yao and Shun, without benevolent government one cannot bring order and peace to the realm. Now there are those who have benevolent hearts and benevolent reputations, yet the people do not receive their blessings, and they cannot serve as models for later generations—this is because they do not put into practice the Way of the former kings.

passages.text: 「故曰，徒善不足以為政，徒法不能以自行。《詩》云：『不愆不忘，率由舊章。』遵先王之法而過者，未之有也。聖人既竭目力焉，繼之以規矩準繩，以為方員平直，不可勝用也；既竭耳力焉，繼之以六律，正五音，不可勝用也；既竭心思焉，繼之以不忍人之政，而仁覆天下矣。
passages.translation_en: "Therefore it is said: goodness alone is not sufficient for governing, and laws alone cannot implement themselves. The Odes say: 'Neither transgressing nor forgetting, following the old statutes.' No one who followed the laws of the former kings ever went astray. When the sages had exhausted the power of their eyes, they supplemented it with compass, square, level, and line to make circles, squares, flat surfaces, and straight lines—these could be used inexhaustibly. When they had exhausted the power of their ears, they supplemented it with the six pitch-pipes to tune the five notes correctly—these could be used inexhaustibly. When they had exhausted the power of their minds, they supplemented it with government that could not bear to see the suffering of others, and benevolence covered the whole realm.

passages.text: 「故曰，為高必因丘陵，為下必因川澤。為政不因先王之道，可謂智乎？是以惟仁者宜在高位。不仁而在高位，是播其惡於眾也。上無道揆也。下無法守也，朝不信道，工不信度，君子犯義，小人犯刑，國之所存者幸也。
passages.translation_en: "Therefore it is said: to build high, one must rely on hills and mounds; to build low, one must rely on rivers and marshes. Can it be called wise to govern without relying on the Way of the former kings? For this reason, only the benevolent should occupy high positions. When someone without benevolence occupies a high position, it is to spread his wickedness among the multitude. When those above have no principles of the Way to guide them, those below have no laws to uphold, the court does not trust the Way, craftsmen do not trust their measures, gentlemen violate righteousness, and common people violate the law—it is sheer luck if the state survives at all.

passages.text: 「故曰，城郭不完，兵甲不多，非國之災也；田野不辟，貨財不聚，非國之害也。上無禮，下無學，賊民興，喪無日矣。《詩》曰：『天之方蹶，無然泄泄。』泄泄，猶沓沓也。事君無義，進退無禮，言則非先王之道者，猶沓沓也。故曰：責難於君謂之恭，陳善閉邪謂之敬，吾君不能謂之賊。」
passages.translation_en: "Therefore it is said: incomplete city walls and a shortage of arms and armor are not the disaster of a state; uncultivated fields and ungathered wealth are not the harm of a state. But when those above lack ritual propriety and those below lack learning, rebellious people will arise, and the state's destruction will come any day. The Odes say: 'Heaven is about to shake things up—do not be so complacent!' Complacent means idle and careless. To serve one's ruler without righteousness, to advance and retire without propriety, and to speak while rejecting the Way of the former kings—that is idle and careless. Therefore it is said: to hold one's ruler to a high standard is called respect; to present what is good and block what is evil is called reverence; to say 'my ruler is incapable' is called being a thief to him."

passages.text: 孟子曰：「規矩，方員之至也；聖人，人倫之至也。欲為君盡君道，欲為臣盡臣道，二者皆法堯舜而已矣。不以舜之所以事堯事君，不敬其君者也；不以堯之所以治民治民，賊其民者也。孔子曰：『道二：仁與不仁而已矣。』暴其民甚，則身弒國亡；不甚，則身危國削。名之曰『幽厲』，雖孝子慈孫，百世不能改也。《詩》云『殷鑒不遠，在夏后之世』，此之謂也。」
passages.translation_en: Mencius said: "The compass and square are the ultimate standard for circles and squares; the sage is the ultimate standard for human relationships. To be a ruler, one must fulfill the Way of a ruler; to be a minister, one must fulfill the Way of a minister—in both cases, one need only take Yao and Shun as models. Not to serve one's ruler as Shun served Yao is to disrespect one's ruler; not to govern the people as Yao governed the people is to rob one's people. Confucius said: 'There are only two paths: benevolence and the lack of benevolence.' A ruler who is excessively cruel to his people will be assassinated and his state will perish; if he is not excessively cruel, he will still be endangered and his state will be diminished. He will be given a posthumous name like 'Dark' or 'Cruel,' and even his filial sons and loving grandsons will not be able to change it for a hundred generations. The Odes say: 'The mirror of Yin is not far off—it lies in the age of the Xia dynasty's heirs.' This is what it means."

passages.text: 孟子曰：「三代之得天下也以仁，其失天下也以不仁。國之所以廢興存亡者亦然。天子不仁，不保四海；諸侯不仁，不保社稷；卿大夫不仁，不保宗廟；士庶人不仁，不保四體。今惡死亡而樂不仁，是猶惡醉而強酒。」孟子曰：「愛人不親反其仁，治人不治反其智，禮人不答反其敬。行有不得者，皆反求諸己，其身正而天下歸之。《詩》云：『永言配命，自求多福。』」
passages.translation_en: Mencius said: "The Three Dynasties won the realm through benevolence, and lost the realm through the lack of benevolence. The same principle applies to why states decline or flourish, survive or perish. If the Son of Heaven is not benevolent, he cannot protect the four seas; if a feudal lord is not benevolent, he cannot protect his altars of soil and grain; if a minister or high official is not benevolent, he cannot protect his ancestral temple; if a gentleman or commoner is not benevolent, he cannot protect his own four limbs. Now, to hate death and ruin yet delight in cruelty is like hating drunkenness yet forcing yourself to drink." Mencius said: "If you love others but they do not respond with affection, examine your own benevolence. If you try to govern others but they remain ungoverned, examine your own wisdom. If you treat others with propriety but they do not reciprocate, examine your own respectfulness. Whenever your actions fail to achieve their aim, always turn inward and examine yourself. When you are upright in yourself, the whole realm will turn to you. The Odes say: 'Always be in accord with Heaven's mandate, and seek your own blessings.'"

passages.text: 孟子曰：「人有恆言，皆曰『天下國家』。天下之本在國，國之本在家，家之本在身。」孟子曰：「為政不難，不得罪於巨室。巨室之所慕，一國慕之；一國之所慕，天下慕之；故沛然德教溢乎四海。」孟子曰：「天下有道，小德役大德，小賢役大賢；天下無道，小役大，弱役強。斯二者天也。順天者存，逆天者亡。齊景公曰：『既不能令，又不受命，是絕物也。』涕出而女於吳。
passages.translation_en: Mencius said: "People have a common saying—they all speak of 'the realm, the state, the family.' The foundation of the realm lies in the state; the foundation of the state lies in the family; the foundation of the family lies in the individual." Mencius said: "Governing is not difficult—do not offend the great families. What the great families admire, the whole state admires; what the whole state admires, the whole realm admires. And so virtue and moral instruction will overflow to fill the four seas." Mencius said: "When the realm has the Way, those of lesser virtue serve those of greater virtue, and those of lesser ability serve those of greater ability. When the realm lacks the Way, the small serve the great, and the weak serve the strong. Both of these are the workings of Heaven. Those who follow Heaven survive; those who go against Heaven perish. Duke Jing of Qi said: 'Since we can neither command others nor accept commands from them, this will cut us off entirely.' He wept as he sent his daughter to marry into the state of Wu.

passages.text: 今也小國師大國而恥受命焉，是猶弟子而恥受命於先師也。如恥之，莫若師文王。師文王，大國五年，小國七年，必為政於天下矣。《詩》云：『商之孫子，其麗不億。上帝既命，侯于周服。侯服于周，天命靡常。殷士膚敏，祼將于京。』孔子曰：『仁不可為眾也。夫國君好仁，天下無敵。』今也欲無敵於天下而不以仁，是猶執熱而不以濯也。《詩》云：『誰能執熱，逝不以濯？』」
passages.translation_en: "Nowadays small states take great states as their teachers yet are ashamed to accept direction from them—this is like a student being ashamed to accept instruction from his teacher. If they feel ashamed, nothing would be better than to take King Wen as their model. Those who model themselves on King Wen—a great state will achieve supremacy in five years, a small state in seven years, and surely will govern the whole realm. The Odes say: 'The descendants of Shang, their numbers were more than hundreds of thousands. But when the Lord on High gave the mandate, they submitted to Zhou. They submitted to Zhou, for Heaven's mandate is not constant. The officers of Yin, elegant and capable, assist with libations in the capital.' Confucius said: 'Benevolence cannot be overcome by mere numbers. If a state's ruler loves benevolence, he will have no rival in the realm.' Now, those who wish to be without rival in the realm yet do not practice benevolence are like those who try to handle something hot without washing their hands in water. The Odes say: 'Who can handle something hot without rinsing with water?'"

passages.text: 孟子曰：「不仁者可與言哉？安其危而利其菑，樂其所以亡者。不仁而可與言，則何亡國敗家之有？有孺子歌曰：『滄浪之水清兮，可以濯我纓；滄浪之水濁兮，可以濯我足。』孔子曰：『小子聽之！清斯濯纓，濁斯濯足矣，自取之也。』夫人必自侮，然後人侮之；家必自毀，而後人毀之；國必自伐，而後人伐之。《太甲》曰：『天作孽，猶可違；自作孽，不可活。』此之謂也。」
passages.translation_en: Mencius said: "Can one even reason with the unbenevolent? They feel secure in their peril, profit from their disasters, and take pleasure in the very things that lead to their ruin. If the unbenevolent could be reasoned with, how would there ever be ruined states and destroyed families? A child's song goes: 'When the waters of the Canglang are clear, I can wash my cap-strings; when the waters of the Canglang are muddy, I can wash my feet.' Confucius said: 'Listen, my young students! When the water is clear, it is used to wash cap-strings; when it is muddy, it is used to wash feet—it brought this on itself.' A person must first demean himself before others demean him; a family must first destroy itself before others destroy it; a state must first attack itself before others attack it. The Tai Jia says: 'When Heaven sends down calamities, one may yet escape them; but when one brings calamity upon oneself, there is no surviving.' This is what it means."

passages.text: 孟子曰：「桀紂之失天下也，失其民也；失其民者，失其心也。得天下有道：得其民，斯得天下矣；得其民有道：得其心，斯得民矣；得其心有道：所欲與之聚之，所惡勿施爾也。民之歸仁也，猶水之就下、獸之走壙也。故為淵敺魚者，獺也；為叢敺爵者，鸇也；為湯武敺民者，桀與紂也。今天下之君有好仁者，則諸侯皆為之敺矣。雖欲無王，不可得已。今之欲王者，猶七年之病求三年之艾也。苟為不畜，終身不得。苟不志於仁，終身憂辱，以陷於死亡。《詩》云『其何能淑，載胥及溺』，此之謂也。」
passages.translation_en: Mencius said: "Jie and Zhou lost the realm because they lost the people; they lost the people because they lost the people's hearts. There is a way to win the realm: win the people, and you win the realm. There is a way to win the people: win their hearts, and you win the people. There is a way to win their hearts: gather for them what they desire, and do not impose on them what they hate. The people turn to benevolence as water flows downward or as animals run to the wilderness. Thus it is the otter that drives fish into the deep waters; it is the hawk that drives birds into the thickets; it was Jie and Zhou who drove the people to Tang and King Wu. If today there were a ruler in the realm who loved benevolence, all the other lords would drive the people to him. Even if he did not wish to become king, he could not avoid it. Those today who wish to become king are like someone with a seven-year illness seeking mugwort that has been dried for three years. If you do not store it up in advance, you will never have it in your whole life. If you do not set your mind on benevolence, you will spend your whole life in anxiety and disgrace, sinking into death and ruin. The Odes say: 'How can they be any good? They will only drag each other into drowning.' This is what it means."

passages.text: 孟子曰：「自暴者，不可與有言也；自棄者，不可與有為也。言非禮義，謂之自暴也；吾身不能居仁由義，謂之自棄也。仁，人之安宅也；義，人之正路也。曠安宅而弗居，舍正路而不由，哀哉！」孟子曰：「道在爾而求諸遠，事在易而求之難。人人親其親、長其長而天下平。」
passages.translation_en: Mencius said: "One who does violence to himself cannot be engaged in conversation; one who throws himself away cannot be engaged in action. To speak against ritual propriety and righteousness is what I call doing violence to oneself; to say 'I am unable to dwell in benevolence and follow righteousness' is what I call throwing oneself away. Benevolence is the peaceful dwelling of a person; righteousness is the proper path of a person. To leave the peaceful dwelling empty and not live in it, to abandon the proper path and not follow it—how sad!" Mencius said: "The Way is near, yet people seek it afar; the task is easy, yet people make it hard. If everyone simply treated their parents as parents and their elders as elders, the whole realm would be at peace."

passages.text: 孟子曰：「居下位而不獲於上，民不可得而治也。獲於上有道：不信於友，弗獲於上矣；信於友有道：事親弗悅，弗信於友矣；悅親有道：反身不誠，不悅於親矣；誠身有道：不明乎善，不誠其身矣。是故誠者，天之道也；思誠者，人之道也。至誠而不動者，未之有也；不誠，未有能動者也。」
passages.translation_en: Mencius said: "If you occupy a low position and do not win the confidence of your superiors, the people cannot be governed. There is a way to win the confidence of your superiors: if your friends do not trust you, you will not win the confidence of your superiors. There is a way to win the trust of your friends: if serving your parents does not please them, you will not win the trust of your friends. There is a way to please your parents: if you reflect on yourself and find a lack of sincerity, you will not please your parents. There is a way to become sincere: if you do not understand what is good, you cannot make yourself sincere. Therefore, sincerity is the Way of Heaven; striving for sincerity is the Way of human beings. There has never been one who was perfectly sincere and yet failed to move others; without sincerity, no one has ever been able to move others."

passages.text: 孟子曰：「伯夷辟紂，居北海之濱，聞文王作，興曰：『盍歸乎來！吾聞西伯善養老者。』太公辟紂，居東海之濱，聞文王作，興曰：『盍歸乎來！吾聞西伯善養老者。』二老者，天下之大老也，而歸之，是天下之父歸之也。天下之父歸之，其子焉往？諸侯有行文王之政者，七年之內，必為政於天下矣。」
passages.translation_en: Mencius said: "Bo Yi fled from the tyrant Zhou and dwelt on the shores of the North Sea. When he heard that King Wen had risen, he stirred and said: 'Why not go home? I have heard that the Chief of the West is good at caring for the elderly.' Tai Gong also fled from Zhou and dwelt on the shores of the East Sea. When he heard that King Wen had risen, he stirred and said: 'Why not go home? I have heard that the Chief of the West is good at caring for the elderly.' These two elders were the most venerable in all the realm, and they turned to King Wen—meaning the fathers of the realm turned to him. When the fathers of the realm turn to someone, where will their sons go? If any feudal lord were to carry out the government of King Wen, within seven years he would surely govern the whole realm."

passages.text: 孟子曰：「求也為季氏宰，無能改於其德，而賦粟倍他日。孔子曰：『求非我徒也，小子鳴鼓而攻之可也。』由此觀之，君不行仁政而富之，皆棄於孔子者也。況於為之強戰？爭地以戰，殺人盈野；爭城以戰，殺人盈城。此所謂率土地而食人肉，罪不容於死。故善戰者服上刑，連諸侯者次之，辟草萊、任土地者次之。」
passages.translation_en: Mencius said: "Ran Qiu served as steward of the Ji family. Unable to improve their virtue, he doubled the grain taxes compared to before. Confucius said: 'Qiu is no disciple of mine. My young students, you may beat the drum and attack him.' From this we can see that any ruler who does not practice benevolent government but is enriched by his ministers—all such ministers were rejected by Confucius. How much more so those who wage aggressive war on his behalf? When wars are fought over territory, the dead fill the fields; when wars are fought over cities, the dead fill the cities. This is what is called leading the land to devour human flesh—a crime for which death is not punishment enough. Therefore those who are skilled at war deserve the heaviest punishment; those who form alliances among the feudal lords for war deserve the next; and those who open up wastelands and exploit the land through heavy taxation deserve the next."

passages.text: 孟子曰：「存乎人者，莫良於眸子。眸子不能掩其惡。胸中正，則眸子瞭焉；胸中不正，則眸子眊焉。聽其言也，觀其眸子，人焉廋哉？」孟子曰：「恭者不侮人，儉者不奪人。侮奪人之君，惟恐不順焉，惡得為恭儉？恭儉豈可以聲音笑貌為哉？」淳于髡曰：「男女授受不親，禮與？」孟子曰：「禮也。」曰：「嫂溺則援之以手乎？」曰：「嫂溺不援，是豺狼也。男女授受不親，禮也；嫂溺援之以手者，權也。」
passages.translation_en: Mencius said: "Of all the features that a person possesses, none is more telling than the pupils of the eyes. The pupils cannot hide a person's wickedness. When one's heart is upright, the pupils are bright and clear; when one's heart is not upright, the pupils are dim and clouded. Listen to a person's words and observe his pupils—how can anyone hide their true self?" Mencius said: "The respectful do not insult others; the frugal do not rob others. A ruler who insults and robs others, constantly fearing only that they will not be obedient—how can he be called respectful or frugal? Can respectfulness and frugality be achieved through mere tone of voice and facial expression?" Chunyu Kun asked: "Is it a rule of propriety that men and women should not touch hands when giving or receiving things?" Mencius said: "It is a rule of propriety." Chunyu Kun said: "If your sister-in-law were drowning, would you pull her out with your hand?" Mencius said: "Not to pull out a drowning sister-in-law would make one a wolf. The rule that men and women should not touch hands when giving or receiving is propriety; pulling out a drowning sister-in-law with your hand is a matter of discretion in extraordinary circumstances."

passages.text: 曰：「今天下溺矣，夫子之不援，何也？」曰：「天下溺，援之以道；嫂溺，援之以手。子欲手援天下乎？」公孫丑曰：「君子之不教子，何也？」孟子曰：「勢不行也。教者必以正；以正不行，繼之以怒；繼之以怒，則反夷矣。『夫子教我以正，夫子未出於正也。』則是父子相夷也。父子相夷，則惡矣。古者易子而教之。父子之間不責善。責善則離，離則不祥莫大焉。」
passages.translation_en: Chunyu Kun said: "Now the whole realm is drowning. Why does the Master not rescue it?" Mencius said: "When the realm is drowning, one rescues it with the Way; when a sister-in-law is drowning, one rescues her with one's hand. Do you want to rescue the entire realm with your bare hand?" Gongsun Chou asked: "Why does a gentleman not teach his own sons?" Mencius said: "The circumstances do not allow it. A teacher must teach by what is correct; when correctness is not followed, anger ensues; when anger ensues, feelings are hurt. The son would think: 'My father teaches me what is correct, yet he himself does not always act correctly.' This leads father and son to hurt each other's feelings, and that is a terrible thing. In ancient times, people exchanged sons and taught each other's children. Between father and son, there should be no demanding of goodness from each other. To demand goodness leads to estrangement, and nothing is more inauspicious than estrangement between father and son."

passages.text: 孟子曰：「事孰為大？事親為大；守孰為大？守身為大。不失其身而能事其親者，吾聞之矣；失其身而能事其親者，吾未之聞也。孰不為事？事親，事之本也；孰不為守？守身，守之本也。曾子養曾皙，必有酒肉。將徹，必請所與。問有餘，必曰『有』。曾皙死，曾元養曾子，必有酒肉。將徹，不請所與。問有餘，曰『亡矣』。將以復進也。此所謂養口體者也。若曾子，則可謂養志也。事親若曾子者，可也。」
passages.translation_en: Mencius said: "Of all forms of service, which is the greatest? Serving one's parents is the greatest. Of all things to guard, which is the greatest? Guarding one's own integrity is the greatest. I have heard of those who, without losing their integrity, were able to serve their parents well; but I have never heard of anyone who, having lost his integrity, was able to serve his parents well. What duty does one not perform? But serving one's parents is the root of all duties. What does one not guard? But guarding one's integrity is the root of all that must be guarded. When Zengzi cared for his father Zeng Xi, there was always wine and meat. When the dishes were about to be cleared, he always asked to whom the leftovers should be given. When asked if there was any left over, he always answered 'Yes.' After Zeng Xi died, when Zeng Yuan cared for Zengzi, there was always wine and meat. But when the dishes were about to be cleared, he did not ask to whom the leftovers should be given. When asked if there was any left over, he answered 'No'—intending to serve the same food again. This is what is called nourishing the mouth and body. Zengzi's way may be called nourishing the will. To serve one's parents as Zengzi did—that is acceptable."

passages.text: 孟子曰：「人不足與適也，政不足間也。惟大人為能格君心之非。君仁莫不仁，君義莫不義，君正莫不正。一正君而國定矣。」孟子曰：「有不虞之譽，有求全之毀。」孟子曰：「人之易其言也，無責耳矣。」孟子曰：「人之患在好為人師。」
passages.translation_en: Mencius said: "It is not worth blaming individual people, nor worth finding fault with particular policies.
