Only a great person can rectify what is wrong in the ruler's heart. When the ruler is benevolent, no one will be unbenevolent; when the ruler is righteous, no one will be unrighteous; when the ruler is upright, no one will fail to be upright. Once the ruler is rectified, the state will be settled." Mencius said: "There is such a thing as unexpected praise, and there is such a thing as fault-finding that demands perfection." Mencius said: "People speak carelessly because they have never been held responsible for their words." Mencius said: "The trouble with people is that they are too fond of being teachers to others."

passages.text: 樂正子從於子敖之齊。樂正子見孟子。孟子曰：「子亦來見我乎？」曰：「先生何為出此言也？」曰：「子來幾日矣？」曰：「昔昔。」曰：「昔昔，則我出此言也，不亦宜乎？」曰：「舍館未定。」曰：「子聞之也，舍館定，然後求見長者乎？」曰：「克有罪。」孟子謂樂正子曰：「子之從於子敖來，徒餔啜也。我不意子學古之道，而以餔啜也。」孟子曰：「不孝有三，無後為大。舜不告而娶，為無後也，君子以為猶告也。」
passages.translation_en: Yue Zhengzi followed Prince Ao to Qi. Yue Zhengzi went to see Mencius. Mencius said: "So you too have come to see me?" Yue Zhengzi said: "Master, why do you say such a thing?" Mencius asked: "How many days have you been here?" Yue Zhengzi replied: "I arrived the day before yesterday." Mencius said: "The day before yesterday? Then is it not fitting that I should say such a thing?" Yue Zhengzi said: "I had not yet settled my lodgings." Mencius said: "Have you ever heard that one must first settle one's lodgings before seeking an audience with an elder?" Yue Zhengzi said: "I was in the wrong." Mencius said to Yue Zhengzi: "You came here following Prince Ao merely for the food and drink. I did not expect that you had studied the Way of the ancients only to pursue food and drink." Mencius said: "There are three things that are unfilial, and having no heir is the greatest. Shun married without telling his parents because he feared having no heir. The gentleman considers this the same as if he had told them."

passages.text: 孟子曰：「仁之實，事親是也；義之實，從兄是也。智之實，知斯二者弗去是也；禮之實，節文斯二者是也；樂之實，樂斯二者，樂則生矣；生則惡可已也，惡可已，則不知足之蹈之、手之舞之。」孟子曰：「天下大悅而將歸己。視天下悅而歸己，猶草芥也。惟舜為然。不得乎親，不可以為人；不順乎親，不可以為子。舜盡事親之道而瞽瞍厎豫，瞽瞍厎豫而天下化，瞽瞍厎豫而天下之為父子者定，此之謂大孝。」
passages.translation_en: Mencius said: "The substance of benevolence is serving one's parents; the substance of righteousness is obeying one's elder brother. The substance of wisdom is to understand these two things and never depart from them; the substance of ritual propriety is to regulate and adorn these two things; the substance of music is to take joy in these two things. When that joy arises, it cannot be stopped; and when it cannot be stopped, one unconsciously begins to dance with one's feet and wave one's hands." Mencius said: "When the whole realm is greatly delighted and is about to turn to you—to regard the whole realm's delight and allegiance as if it were mere grass and rubbish: only Shun was like this. If you cannot win the love of your parents, you cannot be considered a true person; if you cannot be in harmony with your parents, you cannot be considered a true son. Shun exhausted every means of serving his parents, and in the end the Blind Man was pleased. When the Blind Man was pleased, the whole realm was transformed. When the Blind Man was pleased, the standard for the relationship between fathers and sons throughout the realm was set. This is what is called great filial piety."

passages.text: 孟子曰：「舜生於諸馮，遷於負夏，卒於鳴條，東夷之人也。文王生於岐周，卒於畢郢，西夷之人也。地之相去也，千有餘里；世之相後也，千有餘歲。得志行乎中國，若合符節。先聖後聖，其揆一也。」子產聽鄭國之政，以其乘輿濟人於溱洧。孟子曰：「惠而不知為政。歲十一月徒杠成，十二月輿梁成，民未病涉也。君子平其政，行辟人可也。焉得人人而濟之？故為政者，每人而悅之，日亦不足矣。」
passages.translation_en: Mencius said: "Shun was born in Zhufeng, moved to Fuxia, and died in Mingtiao — he was a man of the eastern barbarian regions. King Wen was born in Qizhou and died in Biying — he was a man of the western barbarian regions. Their lands were over a thousand li apart; their eras were over a thousand years apart. Yet when each fulfilled his purpose in the Central States, they matched like the two halves of a tally. The earlier sage and the later sage — their standard was one and the same." Zi Chan managed the government of the state of Zheng, and used his own carriage to ferry people across the Zhen and Wei rivers. Mencius said: "That was kind, but it showed he did not understand governance. If in the eleventh month footbridges are built, and in the twelfth month carriage bridges are completed, the people will not suffer from difficult crossings. When a ruler governs fairly, he may even clear people from his path as he goes out. How can he ferry everyone across personally? Therefore, if a ruler tried to please every single person, he would never have enough hours in the day."

passages.text: 孟子告齊宣王曰：「君之視臣如手足，則臣視君如腹心；君之視臣如犬馬，則臣視君如國人；君之視臣如土芥，則臣視君如寇讎。」王曰：「禮，為舊君有服，何如斯可為服矣？」
passages.translation_en: Mencius said to King Xuan of Qi: "When a ruler regards his ministers as his hands and feet, the ministers regard their ruler as their heart and belly. When the ruler regards his ministers as dogs and horses, the ministers regard their ruler as any common man. When the ruler regards his ministers as dirt and weeds, the ministers regard their ruler as an enemy." The King said: "According to ritual, one wears mourning for a former ruler. Under what conditions does one do so?"

passages.text: 曰：「諫行言聽，膏澤下於民；有故而去，則君使人導之出疆，又先於其所往；去三年不反，然後收其田里。此之謂三有禮焉。如此，則為之服矣。今也為臣。諫則不行，言則不聽；膏澤不下於民；有故而去，則君搏執之，又極之於其所往；去之日，遂收其田里。此之謂寇讎。寇讎何服之有？」孟子曰：「無罪而殺士，則大夫可以去；無罪而戮民，則士可以徙。」孟子曰：「君仁莫不仁，君義莫不義。」孟子曰：「非禮之禮，非義之義，大人弗為。」
passages.translation_en: Mencius said: "When his advice was followed and his words heeded, so that his beneficence flowed down to the people; and when he had reason to leave, the ruler sent an escort to conduct him beyond the border and sent word ahead to his destination; and when after three years he did not return, only then did the ruler reclaim his fields and residence — this is called the three courtesies. Under such conditions, one would wear mourning. But nowadays when serving as a minister, one's advice is not followed and one's words are not heeded; beneficence does not flow down to the people; when one has reason to leave, the ruler seizes and detains him and works to obstruct him at his destination; and on the very day of departure, he immediately reclaims one's fields and residence. This is what is called treating someone as an enemy. What mourning does one owe an enemy?" Mencius said: "When the innocent are killed among the officers, the high ministers may leave. When the innocent are slaughtered among the common people, the officers may relocate." Mencius said: "When the ruler is benevolent, none will be without benevolence. When the ruler is righteous, none will be without righteousness." Mencius said: "Propriety that is not truly proper, righteousness that is not truly right — a great person will have no part in them."

passages.text: 孟子曰：「中也養不中，才也養不才，故人樂有賢父兄也。如中也棄不中，才也棄不才，則賢不肖之相去，其閒不能以寸。」孟子曰：「人有不為也，而後可以有為。」孟子曰：「言人之不善，當如後患何？」孟子曰：「仲尼不為已甚者。」孟子曰：「大人者，言不必信，行不必果，惟義所在。」孟子曰：「大人者，不失其赤子之心者也。」孟子曰：「養生者不足以當大事，惟送死可以當大事。」
passages.translation_en: Mencius said: "Those who have attained the mean nurture those who have not; those who have talent nurture those who lack it. That is why people are glad to have worthy fathers and elder brothers. If those who have attained the mean abandon those who have not, and those with talent abandon those without it, then the distance between the worthy and the unworthy would not be an inch." Mencius said: "Only when a person refrains from certain things can he accomplish great things." Mencius said: "When you speak of others' faults, what will you do when the consequences come?" Mencius said: "Confucius never went to extremes." Mencius said: "A great person does not insist that his words always be believed, nor that his actions always bear fruit — he follows only where righteousness leads." Mencius said: "A great person is one who never loses the heart of a newborn child." Mencius said: "Caring for the living is not enough to count as a great duty; only properly sending off the dead counts as a great duty."

passages.text: 孟子曰：「君子深造之以道，欲其自得之也。自得之，則居之安；居之安，則資之深；資之深，則取之左右逢其原，故君子欲其自得之也。」孟子曰：「博學而詳說之，將以反說約也。」孟子曰：「以善服人者，未有能服人者也；以善養人，然後能服天下。天下不心服而王者，未之有也。」孟子曰：「言無實不祥。不祥之實，蔽賢者當之。」徐子曰：「仲尼亟稱於水，曰：『水哉，水哉！』何取於水也？」
passages.translation_en: Mencius said: "The exemplary person pursues deep mastery through the proper Way, wishing to attain it within himself. When he has attained it within himself, he dwells in it peacefully. When he dwells in it peacefully, he draws upon it deeply. When he draws upon it deeply, he finds its source wherever he turns, left or right. That is why the exemplary person wishes to attain it within himself." Mencius said: "Study broadly and explain in detail, so as to return to what is essential and concise." Mencius said: "One who tries to subdue others through goodness will never succeed in subduing them. But one who nourishes others through goodness can then subdue the whole world. No one has ever ruled the world without winning the hearts of the people." Mencius said: "Words without substance bring misfortune. The substance of that misfortune falls upon those who obstruct the worthy." Xu Zi said: "Confucius repeatedly praised water, saying, 'Water! Water!' What did he find admirable in water?"

passages.text: 孟子曰：「原泉混混，不舍晝夜。盈科而後進，放乎四海，有本者如是，是之取爾。苟為無本，七八月之閒雨集，溝澮皆盈；其涸也，可立而待也。故聲聞過情，君子恥之。」孟子曰：「人之所以異於禽於獸者幾希，庶民去之，君子存之。舜明於庶物，察於人倫，由仁義行，非行仁義也。」
passages.translation_en: Mencius said: "A spring that flows copiously, never ceasing day or night, fills each hollow before moving on, and eventually reaches the four seas. What has a source is like this — that is all he was noting. If something has no source, it is like the rain that collects in the seventh and eighth months, filling all the ditches and gutters — but its drying up can be expected in no time. Therefore, for one's reputation to exceed one's substance is something an exemplary person finds shameful." Mencius said: "What distinguishes human beings from the birds and beasts is but slight. The common people lose it; the exemplary person preserves it. Shun clearly understood the myriad things and had keen insight into human relationships. He acted from benevolence and righteousness, rather than merely performing acts of benevolence and righteousness."

passages.text: 孟子曰：「禹惡旨酒而好善言。湯執中，立賢無方。文王視民如傷，望道而未之見。武王不泄邇，不忘遠。周公思兼三王，以施四事；其有不合者，仰而思之，夜以繼日；幸而得之，坐以待旦。」孟子曰：「王者之迹熄而詩亡，詩亡然後春秋作。晉之乘，楚之檮杌，魯之春秋，一也。其事則齊桓、晉文，其文則史。孔子曰：『其義則丘竊取之矣。』」孟子曰：「君子之澤五世而斬，小人之澤五世而斬。予未得為孔子徒也，予私淑諸人也。」
passages.translation_en: Mencius said: "Yu detested fine wine and loved good counsel. Tang held to the mean and appointed the worthy without regard to their origin. King Wen looked upon the people as if they were wounded, and gazed toward the Way as if he had not yet seen it. King Wu did not neglect those near nor forget those far. The Duke of Zhou aspired to combine the virtues of all three kings and carry out all four of their practices. Whenever something did not accord, he would look upward and think, continuing through the night into the day. When he was fortunate enough to find the answer, he would sit and wait for dawn." Mencius said: "When the traces of the true kings faded, the Odes ceased. When the Odes ceased, the Spring and Autumn Annals was composed. Jin had its Sheng, Chu its Taowu, and Lu its Spring and Autumn — they were all one and the same type of record. Their subject matter was the affairs of Duke Huan of Qi and Duke Wen of Jin, and their style was that of official history. Confucius said: 'As for its moral judgments, I ventured to make those myself.'" Mencius said: "The influence of an exemplary person lasts five generations before it is cut off; the influence of a petty person also lasts five generations before it is cut off. I was not able to be a disciple of Confucius directly — I have refined myself through those who were."

passages.text: 孟子曰：「可以取，可以無取，取傷廉；可以與，可以無與，與傷惠；可以死，可以無死，死傷勇。」
passages.translation_en: Mencius said: "When it is acceptable to take something but also acceptable not to, taking it compromises integrity. When it is acceptable to give something but also acceptable not to, giving compromises generosity. When it is acceptable to die but also acceptable not to, dying compromises courage."

passages.text: 逄蒙學射於羿，盡羿之道，思天下惟羿為愈己，於是殺羿。孟子曰：「是亦羿有罪焉。」公明儀曰：「宜若無罪焉。」曰：「薄乎云爾，惡得無罪？鄭人使子濯孺子侵衛，衛使庾公之斯追之。子濯孺子曰：『今日我疾作，不可以執弓，吾死矣夫！』問其僕曰：『追我者誰也？』其僕曰：『庾公之斯也。』曰：『吾生矣。』其僕曰：『庾公之斯，衛之善射者也，夫子曰「吾生」，何謂也？』曰：『庾公之斯學射於尹公之他，尹公之他學射於我。夫尹公之他，端人也，其取友必端矣。』庾公之斯至，曰：『夫子何為不執弓？』曰：『今日我疾作，不可以執弓。』曰：『小人學射於尹公之他，尹公之他學射於夫子。我不忍以夫子之道反害夫子。雖然，今日之事，君事也，我不敢廢。』抽矢扣輪，去其金，發乘矢而後反。」
passages.translation_en: Feng Meng studied archery under Yi. When he had mastered all of Yi's techniques, he reflected that the only person in the world superior to himself was Yi, and so he killed Yi. Mencius said: "Yi himself bears some blame in this." Gongming Yi said: "It would seem he was blameless." Mencius said: "The blame is slight, that is all — how can he be without blame? The people of Zheng sent Zi Zhuo Ruzi to raid Wei, and Wei sent Yu Gong Zhi Si to pursue him. Zi Zhuo Ruzi said: 'Today my illness has flared up and I cannot hold my bow. I am a dead man!' He asked his charioteer: 'Who is pursuing me?' His charioteer said: 'Yu Gong Zhi Si.' He said: 'Then I shall live.' His charioteer said: 'Yu Gong Zhi Si is the best archer in Wei. How can you say you will live?' He said: 'Yu Gong Zhi Si learned archery from Yin Gong Zhi Ta, and Yin Gong Zhi Ta learned archery from me. Now Yin Gong Zhi Ta is an upright man, and those he befriends must be upright as well.' When Yu Gong Zhi Si arrived, he said: 'Master, why are you not holding your bow?' He said: 'Today my illness has flared up and I cannot hold my bow.' Yu Gong Zhi Si said: 'I learned archery from Yin Gong Zhi Ta, and Yin Gong Zhi Ta learned from you. I cannot bear to use your own art to harm you. Nevertheless, today's affair is my lord's business, and I dare not abandon it.' He drew out his arrows, knocked off their metal tips against the wheel, shot four arrows without their heads, and then turned back."

passages.text: 孟子曰：「西子蒙不潔，則人皆掩鼻而過之。雖有惡人，齊戒沐浴，則可以祀上帝。」孟子曰：「天下之言性也，則故而已矣。故者以利為本。所惡於智者，為其鑿也。如智者若禹之行水也，則無惡於智矣。禹之行水也，行其所無事也。如智者亦行其所無事，則智亦大矣。天之高也，星辰之遠也，苟求其故，千歲之日至，可坐而致也。」
passages.translation_en: Mencius said: "If Xi Shi were smeared with filth, people would all hold their noses passing by. Yet even an ugly person, if he fasts and bathes ritually, may serve in sacrifice to the Lord on High." Mencius said: "When people in the world discuss human nature, they rely on precedent, and precedent takes natural tendency as its basis. What is objectionable in cleverness is its forced contrivance. If the clever were to act as Yu did in channeling water, there would be nothing objectionable in cleverness. Yu channeled water by guiding it along its natural course. If the clever likewise followed the natural course, their wisdom would be great indeed. The heavens are high and the stars are distant, yet if one traces their patterns, the solstices for a thousand years can be calculated while sitting at one's desk."

passages.text: 公行子有子之喪，右師往弔，入門，有進而與右師言者，有就右師之位而與右師言者。孟子不與右師言，右師不悅曰：「諸君子皆與驩言，孟子獨不與驩言，是簡驩也。」孟子聞之，曰：「禮，朝廷不歷位而相與言，不踰階而相揖也。我欲行禮，子敖以我為簡，不亦異乎？」
passages.translation_en: Gong Xing Zi was in mourning for his son. The Right Minister came to pay condolences. When he entered the gate, some went forward to speak with the Right Minister, and others went to where the Right Minister was seated to speak with him. Mencius did not speak with the Right Minister, and the Right Minister was displeased, saying: "All the other gentlemen spoke with Huan, yet Mencius alone did not. He is slighting me." When Mencius heard of this, he said: "According to ritual, at court one does not cross positions to converse, and one does not skip steps to bow. I wished to observe proper ritual, and yet Zi'ao considers me rude — is that not strange?"

passages.text: 孟子曰：「君子所以異於人者，以其存心也。君子以仁存心，以禮存心。仁者愛人，有禮者敬人。愛人者人恆愛之，敬人者人恆敬之。有人於此，其待我以橫逆，則君子必自反也：我必不仁也，必無禮也，此物奚宜至哉？其自反而仁矣，自反而有禮矣，其橫逆由是也，君子必自反也：我必不忠。自反而忠矣，其橫逆由是也，君子曰：『此亦妄人也已矣。如此則與禽獸奚擇哉？於禽獸又何難焉？』是故君子有終身之憂，無一朝之患也。乃若所憂則有之：舜人也，我亦人也。舜為法於天下，可傳於後世，我由未免為鄉人也，是則可憂也。憂之如何？如舜而已矣。若夫君子所患則亡矣。非仁無為也，非禮無行也。如有一朝之患，則君子不患矣。」
passages.translation_en: Mencius said: "What distinguishes the exemplary person from others is what he holds in his heart. The exemplary person holds benevolence in his heart and holds propriety in his heart. The benevolent person loves others; the person of propriety respects others. One who loves others will always be loved by them; one who respects others will always be respected by them. Suppose someone here treats me with violence and insolence. The exemplary person will surely reflect: 'I must have been lacking in benevolence; I must have been lacking in propriety. How else could this have come to me?' If upon reflection he has been benevolent, and upon reflection he has been proper, and the violence and insolence continue, the exemplary person will reflect again: 'I must have been lacking in sincerity.' If upon reflection he has been sincere, and the violence and insolence still continue, the exemplary person says: 'This is simply a deranged person. Being like this, what is there to choose between him and an animal? And why would one take issue with an animal?' Thus the exemplary person has lifelong concern but no momentary anxiety. His concern is this: Shun was a man, and I too am a man. Shun became a model for the world that could be passed down to later generations, while I still amount to nothing more than an ordinary villager — this is worth worrying about. And what does he do about it? He simply strives to be like Shun. As for what an exemplary person might be anxious about — there is nothing. He does nothing that is not benevolent; he does nothing that is not proper. Should some momentary trouble arise, the exemplary person is not troubled by it."

passages.text: 禹、稷當平世，三過其門而不入，孔子賢之。顏子當亂世，居於陋巷。一簞食，一瓢飲。人不堪其憂，顏子不改其樂，孔子賢之。孟子曰：「禹、稷、顏回同道。禹思天下有溺者，由己溺之也；稷思天下有飢者，由己飢之也，是以如是其急也。禹、稷、顏子易地則皆然。今有同室之人鬬者，救之，雖被髮纓冠而救之，可也。鄉鄰有鬬者，被髮纓冠而往救之，則惑也，雖閉戶可也。」
passages.translation_en: Yu and Ji, in a time of peace, passed by their own doors three times without entering, and Confucius praised them for it. Yan Hui, in a time of disorder, lived in a narrow alley. A single bamboo bowl of rice, a single gourd ladle of water — others could not have borne such hardship, yet Yan Hui never changed his joy. Confucius praised him for it. Mencius said: "Yu, Ji, and Yan Hui followed the same Way. Yu felt that if anyone in the world was drowning, it was as if he himself had drowned them. Ji felt that if anyone in the world was starving, it was as if he himself had starved them — that is why they acted with such urgency. If Yu, Ji, and Yan Hui had exchanged positions, each would have done the same as the other. Now suppose someone in your own household is fighting — it is right to rush to the rescue, even with your hair undone and cap untied. But if a neighbor in the village is fighting, to rush out with hair undone and cap untied would be misguided — it would be fine just to bolt your door."

passages.text: 公都子曰：「匡章，通國皆稱不孝焉。夫子與之遊，又從而禮貌之，敢問何也？」
passages.translation_en: Gongdu Zi said: "Kuang Zhang — the whole country calls him unfilial. Yet you, Master, associate with him and even treat him with courtesy. May I ask why?"

passages.text: 孟子曰：「世俗所謂不孝者五：惰其四支，不顧父母之養，一不孝也；博弈好飲酒，不顧父母之養，二不孝也；好貨財，私妻子，不顧父母之養，三不孝也；從耳目之欲，以為父母戮，四不孝也；好勇鬥很，以危父母，五不孝也。章子有一於是乎？夫章子，子父責善而不相遇也。責善，朋友之道也；父子責善，賊恩之大者。夫章子，豈不欲有夫妻子母之屬哉？為得罪於父，不得近。出妻屏子，終身不養焉。其設心以為不若是，是則罪之大者，是則章子已矣。
passages.translation_en: Mencius said: "There are five things the world conventionally calls unfilial: Laziness of limb, neglecting the support of one's parents — this is the first. Indulgence in chess and drinking, neglecting the support of one's parents — this is the second. Love of wealth and favoritism toward wife and children, neglecting the support of one's parents — this is the third. Indulging the desires of the eyes and ears, bringing disgrace upon one's parents — this is the fourth. Being fond of bravery and fighting, thereby endangering one's parents — this is the fifth. Does Zhang have any of these? Zhang and his father fell out over the insistence on goodness between them. Insisting on goodness is the way of friends; between father and son, insisting on goodness is the greatest injury to affection. Did Zhang not wish to have the bonds of husband and wife, parent and child? But having offended his father, he could not draw near, so he sent away his wife, put aside his son, and to the end of his life received no care from them. In his heart he felt that to do anything less would be an even greater wrong. Such is the case of Zhang."

passages.text: 曾子居武城，有越寇。或曰：「寇至，盍去諸？」曰：「無寓人於我室，毀傷其薪木。」寇退，則曰：「修我牆屋，我將反。」寇退，曾子反。左右曰：「待先生，如此其忠且敬也。寇至則先去以為民望，寇退則反，殆於不可。」沈猶行曰：「是非汝所知也。昔沈猶有負芻之禍，從先生者七十人，未有與焉。」子思居於衛，有齊寇。或曰：「寇至，盍去諸？」子思曰：「如伋去，君誰與守？」
passages.translation_en: Zengzi lived in Wucheng when there was a raid from Yue. Someone said: "The raiders are coming — should you not leave?" He said: "Do not let anyone lodge in my house or damage the trees and shrubs." When the raiders withdrew, he said: "Repair my walls and roof — I shall return." When the raiders withdrew, Zengzi returned. His attendants said: "You were treated by the people with such loyalty and respect, yet when the raiders came you were the first to leave, setting an example for the people, and when they withdrew you returned. This seems not quite right." Shen Youxing said: "This is beyond your understanding. In the past, Shen You faced the calamity of the firewood carrier. Of the seventy followers of the Master, not one was involved in it." Zi Si was living in Wei when there was a raid from Qi. Someone said: "The raiders are coming — should you not leave?" Zi Si said: "If I leave, with whom will the ruler defend the state?"

passages.text: 孟子曰：「曾子、子思同道。曾子，師也，父兄也；子思，臣也，微也。曾子、子思易地則皆然。」儲子曰：「王使人瞷夫子，果有以異於人乎？」孟子曰：「何以異於人哉？堯舜與人同耳。」齊人有一妻一妾而處室者，其良人出，則必饜酒肉而後反。其妻問所與飲食者，則盡富貴也。其妻告其妾曰：「良人出，則必饜酒肉而後反；問其與飲食者，盡富貴也，而未嘗有顯者來，吾將瞷良人之所之也。」
passages.translation_en: Mencius said: "Zengzi and Zi Si followed the same Way. Zengzi was a teacher, in the role of father and elder brother. Zi Si was a minister, in a humble position. If Zengzi and Zi Si had exchanged positions, each would have done the same." Chu Zi said: "The King sent someone to observe you, Master, to see if there is truly something different about you compared to other people." Mencius said: "How would I be different from other people? Yao and Shun were the same as everyone else." A man of Qi had a wife and a concubine and lived with them. Whenever the husband went out, he would always come home stuffed with wine and meat. When his wife asked who he had been eating and drinking with, they were all wealthy and distinguished people. His wife said to the concubine: "When our husband goes out, he always returns full of wine and meat. When I ask who he dined with, they are all wealthy and distinguished. Yet no distinguished person has ever come to visit us. I am going to secretly follow our husband and see where he goes."

passages.text: 蚤起，施從良人之所之，遍國中無與立談者。卒之東郭墦閒，之祭者，乞其餘；不足，又顧而之他，此其為饜足之道也。其妻歸，告其妾曰：「良人者，所仰望而終身也。今若此。」與其妾訕其良人，而相泣於中庭。而良人未之知也，施施從外來，驕其妻妾。由君子觀之，則人之所以求富貴利達者，其妻妾不羞也，而不相泣者，幾希矣。
passages.translation_en: She rose early and stealthily followed her husband to where he went. Throughout the entire city, not a single person stopped to talk with him. Finally he went among the tombs on the eastern outskirts, approaching those who were making offerings and begging for their leftovers. When that was not enough, he looked around and went to others. This was how he got his fill. His wife went home and told the concubine: "A husband is someone you look up to for the rest of your life. And now it has come to this." Together with the concubine she berated her husband, and they wept together in the courtyard. Meanwhile, the husband knew nothing of this and came swaggering in from outside, preening before his wife and concubine. From the perspective of an exemplary person, as for the means by which people pursue wealth, rank, and advancement — few are those whose wives and concubines would not be ashamed and weep.

passages.text: 萬章問曰：「舜往于田，號泣于旻天，何為其號泣也？」孟子曰：「怨慕也。」萬章曰：「父母愛之，喜而不忘；父母惡之，勞而不怨。然則舜怨乎？」
passages.translation_en: Wan Zhang asked: "When Shun went to the fields and wept and cried out to compassionate Heaven, why did he weep and cry out?" Mencius said: "Out of resentful longing." Wan Zhang said: "When parents love you, you rejoice and never forget them; when parents dislike you, you toil without resentment. Was Shun then resentful?"

passages.text: 曰：「長息問於公明高曰：『舜往于田，則吾既得聞命矣；號泣于旻天，于父母，則吾不知也。』公明高曰：『是非爾所知也。』夫公明高以孝子之心，為不若是恝，我竭力耕田，共為子職而已矣，父母之不我愛，於我何哉？帝使其子九男二女，百官牛羊倉廩備，以事舜於畎畝之中。天下之士多就之者，帝將胥天下而遷之焉。為不順於父母，如窮人無所歸。天下之士悅之，人之所欲也，而不足以解憂；好色，人之所欲，妻帝之二女，而不足以解憂；富，人之所欲，富有天下，而不足以解憂；貴，人之所欲，貴為天子，而不足以解憂。人悅之、好色、富貴，無足以解憂者，惟順於父母，可以解憂。人少，則慕父母；知好色，則慕少艾；有妻子，則慕妻子；仕則慕君，不得於君則熱中。大孝終身慕父母。五十而慕者，予於大舜見之矣。」
passages.translation_en: Mencius said: "Chang Xi once asked Gongming Gao: 'That Shun went to the fields — I have heard your explanation of that. But that he wept and cried out to compassionate Heaven and to his parents — that I do not understand.' Gongming Gao replied: 'This is beyond your comprehension.' In Gongming Gao's view, a filial son's heart could not be so indifferent as to say: 'I have done my best to plow the fields and fulfill my duty as a son — that is all. If my parents do not love me, what concern is that of mine?' The Emperor sent his nine sons and two daughters, along with a full complement of officials, oxen, sheep, and granaries, to serve Shun amid the fields. Most of the scholars in the realm went to join him, and the Emperor was prepared to hand over the entire realm to him. Yet because he could not gain the approval of his parents, Shun was like a destitute man with nowhere to turn. The admiration of all the scholars in the realm — something everyone desires — was not enough to relieve his sorrow. Beautiful women — something everyone desires — and being married to the Emperor's two daughters was not enough to relieve his sorrow. Wealth — something everyone desires — and possessing all the wealth of the realm was not enough to relieve his sorrow. Honor — something everyone desires — and being honored as the Son of Heaven was not enough to relieve his sorrow. The admiration of others, beautiful women, wealth, and honor — none of these could relieve his sorrow. Only gaining the approval of his parents could relieve it. When young, a person longs for his parents. When he becomes aware of the attraction of beauty, he longs for young and lovely women. When he has a wife and children, he longs for his wife and children. When he enters public service, he longs for his sovereign, and if he fails to gain his sovereign's favor, he burns with anxiety. But a person of the greatest filial devotion longs for his parents his entire life. In the great Shun, even at fifty still longing for his parents — there I see such devotion."

passages.text: 萬章問曰：「《詩》云：『娶妻如之何？必告父母。』信斯言也，宜莫如舜。舜之不告而娶，何也？」孟子曰：「告則不得娶。男女居室，人之大倫也。如告，則廢人之大倫，以懟父母，是以不告也。」萬章曰：「舜之不告而娶，則吾既得聞命矣；帝之妻舜而不告，何也？」曰：「帝亦知告焉則不得妻也。」
passages.translation_en: Wan Zhang asked: "The Odes say: 'How should one take a wife? One must first inform one's parents.' If anyone should have believed these words, surely it was Shun. Yet Shun married without informing his parents — why?" Mencius said: "Had he informed them, he would not have been allowed to marry. The union of man and woman in marriage is the greatest of human relationships. Had he informed them, he would have had to abandon this greatest of human relationships, which would have bred resentment toward his parents. That is why he did not inform them." Wan Zhang said: "That Shun did not inform his parents before marrying — I have heard your explanation of that. But why did the Emperor give his daughters to Shun without informing Shun's parents?" Mencius said: "The Emperor also knew that if he informed them, the marriage would not be permitted."

passages.text: 萬章曰：「父母使舜完廩，捐階，瞽瞍焚廩。使浚井，出，從而揜之。象曰：『謨蓋都君咸我績。牛羊父母，倉廩父母，干戈朕，琴朕，弤朕，二嫂使治朕棲。』象往入舜宮，舜在床琴。象曰：『鬱陶思君爾。』忸怩。舜曰：『惟茲臣庶，汝其于予治。』不識舜不知象之將殺己與？」曰：「奚而不知也？象憂亦憂，象喜亦喜。」曰：「然則舜偽喜者與？」
passages.translation_en: Wan Zhang said: "Shun's parents sent him to repair the granary roof, then removed the ladder, and the Blind Man set fire to the granary. They sent him to dredge a well, and after he climbed out, they covered it over. Xiang said: 'The credit for plotting to bury our lord-like brother is all mine! The oxen and sheep shall go to Father and Mother, the granaries to Father and Mother. The shields and spears shall be mine, the lute shall be mine, the carved bow shall be mine, and I shall make the two sisters-in-law attend to my bed.' Xiang went into Shun's palace, and there was Shun sitting on the bed playing the lute. Xiang said: 'I have been thinking of you with deep longing,' but he looked embarrassed. Shun said: 'I have all these subjects and officials — please help me govern them.' I wonder, did Shun not know that Xiang intended to kill him?" Mencius said: "How could he not know? When Xiang was troubled, Shun was troubled; when Xiang was happy, Shun was happy." Wan Zhang said: "Then was Shun's happiness merely pretended?"

passages.text: 曰：「否。昔者有饋生魚於鄭子產，子產使校人畜之池。校人烹之，反命曰：『始舍之圉圉焉，少則洋洋焉，攸然而逝。』子產曰『得其所哉！得其所哉！』校人出，曰：『孰謂子產智？予既烹而食之，曰：得其所哉？得其所哉。』故君子可欺以其方，難罔以非其道。彼以愛兄之道來，故誠信而喜之，奚偽焉？」萬章問曰：「象日以殺舜為事，立為天子，則放之，何也？」孟子曰：「封之也，或曰放焉。」
passages.translation_en: Mencius said: "No. In ancient times, someone sent a gift of live fish to Zi Chan of Zheng. Zi Chan ordered the pond keeper to raise them in the pond. The pond keeper cooked and ate them instead, then reported back: 'When I first released them they were sluggish, but soon they became lively and swam off happily into the deep.' Zi Chan said: 'They found their place! They found their place!' The pond keeper went out and said: 'Who says Zi Chan is clever? I cooked and ate them, and he said: They found their place! They found their place!' Thus a gentleman can be deceived by what accords with principle, but cannot be fooled by what violates it. Xiang came to Shun with the manner of one who loves his brother, and so Shun genuinely believed him and was happy — what pretense was there?" Wan Zhang asked: "Xiang made it his daily business to try to kill Shun. When Shun became Son of Heaven, why did he merely exile Xiang?" Mencius said: "He enfeoffed him — though some say it was exile."

passages.text: 萬章曰：「舜流共工于幽州，放驩兜于崇山，殺三苗于三危，殛鯀于羽山，四罪而天下咸服，誅不仁也。象至不仁，封之有庳。有庳之人奚罪焉？仁人固如是乎？在他人則誅之，在弟則封之。」曰：「仁人之於弟也，不藏怒焉，不宿怨焉，親愛之而已矣。親之欲其貴也，愛之欲其富也。封之有庳，富貴之也。身為天子，弟為匹夫，可謂親愛之乎？」「敢問或曰放者，何謂也？」
passages.translation_en: Wan Zhang said: "Shun banished Gong Gong to You Zhou, exiled Huan Dou to Chong Mountain, destroyed the San Miao at San Wei, and executed Gun on Yu Mountain. These four were punished and the whole realm submitted, for it was the punishment of the wicked. Yet Xiang was the most wicked of all, and Shun enfeoffed him in You Bi. What had the people of You Bi done to deserve that? Is this how a benevolent man acts — punishing wickedness in others but enfeoffing it in his own brother?" Mencius said: "A benevolent man does not harbor anger or nurse grudges against his brother — he simply loves him with familial affection. Loving him, he wishes him to be honored; being affectionate toward him, he wishes him to be wealthy. Enfeoffing him in You Bi was to give him both wealth and honor. If Shun were Son of Heaven while his brother remained a commoner, could that be called familial love?" Wan Zhang asked: "May I ask what those who call it exile mean?"

passages.text: 曰：「象不得有為於其國，天子使吏治其國，而納其貢稅焉，故謂之放，豈得暴彼民哉？雖然，欲常常而見之，故源源而來。『不及貢，以政接于有庳』，此之謂也。」咸丘蒙問曰：「語云：『盛德之士，君不得而臣，父不得而子。』舜南面而立，堯帥諸侯北面而朝之，瞽瞍亦北面而朝之。舜見瞽瞍，其容有蹙。孔子曰：『於斯時也，天下殆哉，岌岌乎！』不識此語誠然乎哉？」
passages.translation_en: Mencius said: "Xiang was not permitted to govern his own state. The Son of Heaven appointed officials to administer the state and collect its tribute and taxes. That is why some called it exile — for how could he be allowed to tyrannize the people? Even so, Shun wished to see him constantly, and so Xiang came to court in a steady stream. The phrase 'not waiting for the regular tribute period, he conducted governance through visits to You Bi' refers to this." Xianqiu Meng asked: "A saying goes: 'A man of supreme virtue cannot be treated as a subject by his sovereign, nor as a son by his father.' When Shun faced south as ruler, Yao led the feudal lords to face north and pay court to him, and the Blind Man also faced north and paid court. When Shun received the Blind Man, his expression was uneasy. Confucius said: 'At that moment, the realm was in peril — truly precarious!' Is this saying really true?"

passages.text: 孟子曰：「否。此非君子之言，齊東野人之語也。堯老而舜攝也。《堯典》曰：『二十有八載，放勳乃徂落，百姓如喪考妣，三年，四海遏密八音。』孔子曰：『天無二日，民無二王。』舜既為天子矣，又帥天下諸侯以為堯三年喪，是二天子矣。」咸丘蒙曰：「舜之不臣堯，則吾既得聞命矣。《詩》云：『普天之下，莫非王土；率土之濱，莫非王臣。』而舜既為天子矣，敢問瞽瞍之非臣，如何？」
passages.translation_en: Mencius said: "No. These are not the words of a gentleman — they are the talk of rustic folk east of Qi. When Yao was old, Shun served as regent. The 'Canon of Yao' says: 'After twenty-eight years, Fang Xun passed away. The hundred families mourned as if for their own parents. For three years, throughout the four seas, all music was silenced.' Confucius said: 'Heaven does not have two suns; the people do not have two kings.' If Shun had already become Son of Heaven and then also led the feudal lords of the realm in observing three years of mourning for Yao, there would have been two Sons of Heaven at once." Xianqiu Meng said: "That Shun did not treat Yao as a subject — I have heard your explanation of that. But the Odes say: 'Under all of heaven, there is no land that is not the king's; to the borders of the land, there is no one who is not the king's subject.' Since Shun had become Son of Heaven, may I ask how the Blind Man could not be his subject?"

passages.text: 曰：「是詩也，非是之謂也；勞於王事，而不得養父母也。曰：『此莫非王事，我獨賢勞也。』故說《詩》者，不以文害辭，不以辭害志。以意逆志，是為得之。如以辭而已矣，《雲漢》之詩曰：『周餘黎民，靡有孑遺。』信斯言也，是周無遺民也。孝子之至，莫大乎尊親；尊親之至，莫大乎以天下養。為天子父，尊之至也；以天下養，養之至也。《詩》曰：『永言孝思，孝思維則。』此之謂也。《書》曰：『祗載見瞽瞍，夔夔齊栗，瞽瞍亦允若。』是為父不得而子也。」
passages.translation_en: Mencius said: "That poem does not mean what you think. It is about someone laboring at the king's business and being unable to care for his parents. He says: 'All of these are the king's affairs, yet I alone bear this heavy burden.' Therefore, in interpreting the Odes, one must not let the literal words distort the phrases, nor let the phrases distort the intended meaning. One should use one's own understanding to trace back to the author's intent — that is the way to grasp it. If one went only by the literal words, then the poem 'Yun Han' in the Odes says: 'Of the remaining multitudes of Zhou, not a single one survived.' If we believed this literally, it would mean that not a single person was left in Zhou. The highest expression of a filial son is nothing greater than honoring his parents. The highest expression of honoring one's parents is nothing greater than supporting them with the whole realm. To be the father of the Son of Heaven — that is the ultimate in honor. To be supported with the whole realm — that is the ultimate in support. The Odes say: 'Forever cherishing filial thoughts — those filial thoughts are a model for all.' This is what it refers to. The Documents say: 'Respectfully and reverently, Shun appeared before the Blind Man, full of awe and trembling — and the Blind Man also was brought to trust and comply.' This is what it means for a father not to be able to treat his son as merely a son."

passages.text: 萬章曰：「堯以天下與舜，有諸？」孟子曰：「否。天子不能以天下與人。」「然則舜有天下也，孰與之？」曰：「天與之。」「天與之者，諄諄然命之乎？」曰：「否。天不言，以行與事示之而已矣。」曰：「以行與事示之者如之何？」
passages.translation_en: Wan Zhang said: "Did Yao give the realm to Shun? Is this true?" Mencius said: "No. The Son of Heaven cannot give the realm to another person." "Then if Shun possessed the realm, who gave it to him?" Mencius said: "Heaven gave it to him." "When Heaven gave it to him, did Heaven instruct him with repeated and explicit commands?" Mencius said: "No. Heaven does not speak — it simply reveals its will through actions and affairs."  Wan Zhang said: "How does Heaven reveal its will through actions and affairs?"

passages.text: 曰：「天子能薦人於天，不能使天與之天下；諸侯能薦人於天子，不能使天子與之諸侯；大夫能薦人於諸侯，不能使諸侯與之大夫。昔者堯薦舜於天而天受之，暴之於民而民受之，故曰：天不言，以行與事示之而已矣。」曰：「敢問薦之於天而天受之，暴之於民而民受之，如何？」
passages.translation_en: Mencius said: "The Son of Heaven can recommend a person to Heaven, but cannot make Heaven give that person the realm. A feudal lord can recommend a person to the Son of Heaven, but cannot make the Son of Heaven give that person a fief. A minister can recommend a person to a feudal lord, but cannot make the feudal lord give that person a ministry. In ancient times, Yao recommended Shun to Heaven, and Heaven accepted him. He presented Shun to the people, and the people accepted him. Therefore I say: Heaven does not speak — it simply reveals its will through actions and affairs." Wan Zhang said: "May I ask how Heaven accepted him when he was recommended to Heaven, and how the people accepted him when he was presented to the people?"

passages.text: 曰：「使之主祭而百神享之，是天受之；使之主事而事治，百姓安之，是民受之也。天與之，人與之，故曰：天子不能以天下與人。舜相堯二十有八載，非人之所能為也，天也。堯崩，三年之喪畢，舜避堯之子於南河之南。天下諸侯朝覲者，不之堯之子而之舜；訟獄者，不之堯之子而之舜；謳歌者，不謳歌堯之子而謳歌舜，故曰天也。夫然後之中國，踐天子位焉。而居堯之宮，逼堯之子，是篡也，非天與也。《太誓》曰：『天視自我民視，天聽自我民聽』，此之謂也。」
passages.translation_en: Mencius said: "Yao had Shun preside over the sacrifices, and all the spirits received them with satisfaction — this was Heaven accepting him. He had Shun preside over affairs, and affairs were well governed and the people were at peace — this was the people accepting him. Heaven gave it to him, and the people gave it to him. That is why I say the Son of Heaven cannot give the realm to another person. Shun served as Yao's minister for twenty-eight years — this was not something any human could have brought about; it was Heaven. When Yao died and the three years of mourning were complete, Shun withdrew from Yao's son to the south of the Southern River. Yet the feudal lords of the realm who came to pay court went not to Yao's son but to Shun. Those with legal disputes went not to Yao's son but to Shun. Those who sang songs of praise sang not of Yao's son but of Shun. Therefore I say it was Heaven. Only after this did Shun go to the central kingdom and assume the position of Son of Heaven. Had he simply occupied Yao's palace and pushed aside Yao's son, that would have been usurpation, not the gift of Heaven. The 'Great Declaration' says: 'Heaven sees through the eyes of my people; Heaven hears through the ears of my people.' This is what it means."

passages.text: 萬章問曰：「人有言：『至於禹而德衰，不傳於賢而傳於子。』有諸？」
passages.translation_en: Wan Zhang asked: "People say: 'When it came to Yu, virtue had declined — the realm was not transmitted to the worthiest but to his own son.' Is this true?"

passages.text: 孟子曰：「否，不然也。天與賢，則與賢；天與子，則與子。昔者舜薦禹於天，十有七年，舜崩。三年之喪畢，禹避舜之子於陽城。天下之民從之，若堯崩之後，不從堯之子而從舜也。禹薦益於天，七年，禹崩。三年之喪畢，益避禹之子於箕山之陰。朝覲訟獄者不之益而之啟，曰：『吾君之子也。』謳歌者不謳歌益而謳歌啟，曰：『吾君之子也。』丹朱之不肖，舜之子亦不肖。舜之相堯，禹之相舜也，歷年多，施澤於民久。啟賢，能敬承繼禹之道。益之相禹也，歷年少，施澤於民未久。舜、禹、益相去久遠，其子之賢不肖，皆天也，非人之所能為也。莫之為而為者，天也；莫之致而至者，命也。匹夫而有天下者，德必若舜禹，而又有天子薦之者，故仲尼不有天下。繼世以有天下，天之所廢，必若桀紂者也，故益、伊尹、周公不有天下。伊尹相湯以王於天下。湯崩，太丁未立，外丙二年，仲壬四年。太甲顛覆湯之典刑，伊尹放之於桐。三年，太甲悔過，自怨自艾，於桐處仁遷義；三年，以聽伊尹之訓己也，復歸于亳。周公之不有天下，猶益之於夏，伊尹之於殷也。孔子曰：『唐虞禪，夏后、殷、周繼，其義一也。』」
passages.translation_en: Mencius said: "No, that is not so. When Heaven gives the realm to the worthiest, it goes to the worthiest; when Heaven gives it to a son, it goes to the son. In ancient times, Shun recommended Yu to Heaven. Seventeen years later, Shun died. When the three years of mourning were complete, Yu withdrew from Shun's son to Yang Cheng. The people of the realm followed him, just as after Yao's death they had followed Shun rather than Yao's son. Yu recommended Yi to Heaven. Seven years later, Yu died. When the three years of mourning were complete, Yi withdrew from Yu's son to the north of Ji Mountain. But those who came to pay court and bring legal disputes went not to Yi but to Qi, saying: 'He is our lord's son.' Those who sang songs of praise sang not of Yi but of Qi, saying: 'He is our lord's son.' Yao's son Dan Zhu was unworthy, and Shun's son was also unworthy. Shun's service as minister to Yao and Yu's service as minister to Shun lasted many years, and their blessings to the people endured long. Qi was worthy and able to respectfully carry on Yu's way. Yi's service as minister to Yu lasted few years, and his blessings to the people had not endured long. The great distances in time between Shun, Yu, and Yi, and the worthiness or unworthiness of their sons — all of this was Heaven's doing, not something humans could bring about. What comes about without anyone making it happen is Heaven. What arrives without anyone summoning it is fate. For a commoner to possess the realm, his virtue must equal that of Shun or Yu, and he must also have the recommendation of a Son of Heaven — that is why Confucius did not possess the realm. For one who inherits the realm through succession to be deposed by Heaven, he must be as wicked as Jie or Zhou — that is why Yi, Yi Yin, and the Duke of Zhou did not possess the realm. Yi Yin served as minister to Tang and helped him become king over the realm. When Tang died, Tai Ding had not yet been installed. Wai Bing reigned for two years and Zhong Ren for four. Then Tai Jia overturned the statutes and standards of Tang, and Yi Yin banished him to Tong. After three years, Tai Jia repented of his errors, blamed himself and reformed, and while at Tong he cultivated benevolence and moved toward righteousness. After three years of heeding Yi Yin's instructions, he was restored to Bo. The Duke of Zhou's not possessing the realm was like Yi's case with the Xia and Yi Yin's case with the Yin. Confucius said: 'The abdications of Tang and Yu, and the hereditary successions of the Xia, Yin, and Zhou — the principle behind them is one and the same.'"

passages.text: 萬章問曰：「人有言『伊尹以割烹要湯』有諸？」
passages.translation_en: Wan Zhang asked: "People say that Yi Yin sought an audience with Tang by means of his skills as a cook. Is this true?"

passages.text: 孟子曰：「否，不然。伊尹耕於有莘之野，而樂堯舜之道焉。非其義也，非其道也，祿之以天下，弗顧也；繫馬千駟，弗視也。非其義也，非其道也，一介不以與人，一介不以取諸人，湯使人以幣聘之，囂囂然曰：『我何以湯之聘幣為哉？我豈若處畎畝之中，由是以樂堯舜之道哉？』湯三使往聘之，既而幡然改曰：『與我處畎畝之中，由是以樂堯舜之道，吾豈若使是君為堯舜之君哉？吾豈若使是民為堯舜之民哉？吾豈若於吾身親見之哉？天之生此民也，使先知覺後知，使先覺覺後覺也。予，天民之先覺者也；予將以斯道覺斯民也。非予覺之，而誰也？』思天下之民匹夫匹婦有不被堯舜之澤者，若己推而內之溝中。其自任以天下之重如此，故就湯而說之以伐夏救民。吾未聞枉己而正人者也，況辱己以正天下者乎？聖人之行不同也，或遠或近，或去或不去，歸潔其身而已矣。吾聞其以堯舜之道要湯，未聞以割烹也。伊訓曰：『天誅造攻自牧宮，朕載自亳。』」
passages.translation_en: Mencius said: "No, that is not so. This is the fabrication of meddlesome people. Yi Yin was farming in the wilds of the state of You Xin, and he delighted in the Way of Yao and Shun. If something was contrary to righteousness or contrary to the Way, even if you offered him the revenues of the whole realm, he would pay no attention; even if you tethered four thousand horses before him, he would not give them a glance. If something was contrary to righteousness or contrary to the Way, he would neither give so much as a trifle to another person nor take so much as a trifle from another person. Tang sent envoys with gifts to invite him. He said contentedly: 'What would I do with Tang's gifts? Would I not rather stay here amid the fields and delight in the Way of Yao and Shun?' Only after Tang sent envoys three times did he change his mind and say: 'Rather than staying amid the fields delighting in the Way of Yao and Shun, would it not be better to make this sovereign into a sovereign like Yao or Shun? Would it not be better to make these people into people like those of Yao or Shun? Would it not be better to see this with my own eyes in my own lifetime? Heaven, in producing these people, intended those who understand first to awaken those who understand later, and those who are aware first to awaken those who are aware later. I am one of Heaven's people who has been among the first to be awakened. I shall use this Way to awaken this people. If not I, then who?' He thought that if among the common men and women of the realm there were any who had not received the blessings of Yao and Shun, it was as if he himself had pushed them into a ditch. Such was the weight of responsibility he took upon himself for the whole realm. And so he went to Tang and persuaded him to launch the campaign against the Xia to save the people. I have never heard of someone who bends himself being able to straighten others — how much less someone who disgraces himself in order to set the realm right. The actions of sages differ — some stay far away, some stay near; some depart, some remain — but all alike return to keeping their persons pure. I have heard that Yi Yin sought Tang's attention through the Way of Yao and Shun; I have not heard that he did so through cooking. The 'Instructions of Yi' says: 'Heaven's punishment was to be carried out, beginning from the Mu Palace. I, for my part, began from Bo.'"

passages.text: 萬章問曰：「或謂孔子於衛主癰疽，於齊主侍人瘠環，有諸乎？」
passages.translation_en: Wan Zhang asked: "Some say that when Confucius was in Wei, he lodged with the court eunuch Yong Ju, and when in Qi, he lodged with the attendant Ji Huan. Is this true?"

passages.text: 孟子曰：「否，不然也。好事者為之也。於衛主顏讎由。彌子之妻與子路之妻，兄弟也。彌子謂子路曰：『孔子主我，衛卿可得也。』子路以告。孔子曰：『有命。』孔子進以禮，退以義，得之不得曰『有命』。而主癰疽與侍人瘠環，是無義無命也。孔子悅於魯衛，遭宋桓司馬將要而殺之，微服而過宋。是時孔子當阨，主司城貞子，為陳侯周臣。吾聞觀近臣，以其所為主；觀遠臣，以其所主。若孔子主癰疽與侍人瘠環，何以為孔子？」
passages.translation_en: Mencius said: "No, that is not so. This is the fabrication of meddlesome people. In Wei, Confucius lodged with Yan Chou You. The wife of Mi Zi and the wife of Zi Lu were sisters. Mi Zi said to Zi Lu: 'If Confucius lodges with me, he can obtain the position of minister of Wei.' Zi Lu reported this to Confucius. Confucius said: 'That is a matter of fate.' Confucius advanced according to propriety and withdrew according to righteousness. Whether he obtained office or not, he said: 'That is a matter of fate.' Had he lodged with the eunuch Yong Ju or the attendant Ji Huan, that would have been to abandon both righteousness and fate. When Confucius was out of favor in both Lu and Wei, he encountered the Song minister of war Huan Tui, who plotted to intercept and kill him. He passed through Song in disguise. At that time, Confucius was in dire straits and lodged with Sicheng Zhen Zi, who was a minister of the Marquis of Chen. I have heard that one judges a minister at court by whom he serves, and a minister abroad by whom he lodges with. If Confucius had lodged with the eunuch Yong Ju and the attendant Ji Huan, how could he have been Confucius?"

passages.text: 萬章問曰：「或曰：『百里奚自鬻於秦養牲者，五羊之皮，食牛，以要秦穆公。』信乎？」
passages.translation_en: Wan Zhang asked: "Some say: 'Baili Xi sold himself to a cattle feeder of Qin for five ram skins, and fed cattle in order to gain an audience with Duke Mu of Qin.' Is this true?"

passages.text: 孟子曰：「否，不然。好事者為之也。百里奚，虞人也。晉人以垂棘之璧與屈產之乘，假道於虞以伐虢。宮之奇諫，百里奚不諫。知虞公之不可諫而去，之秦，年已七十矣，曾不知以食牛干秦穆公之為汙也，可謂智乎？不可諫而不諫，可謂不智乎？知虞公之將亡而先去之，不可謂不智也。時舉於秦，知穆公之可與有行也而相之，可謂不智乎？相秦而顯其君於天下，可傳於後世，不賢而能之乎？自鬻以成其君，鄉黨自好者不為，而謂賢者為之乎？」
passages.translation_en: Mencius said: "No, that is not so. This is the fabrication of meddlesome people. Baili Xi was a man of the state of Yu. The state of Jin offered the Chuiji jade disc and horses from Qu to borrow passage through Yu in order to attack Guo. Gong Zhi Qi remonstrated against granting passage, but Baili Xi did not remonstrate. He knew the Duke of Yu could not be remonstrated with, so he left and went to Qin. He was already seventy years old. If he still did not know that feeding cattle to seek an audience with Duke Mu of Qin would be degrading — could he be called wise? Yet by not remonstrating when remonstrance was impossible, can he be called unwise? He knew that the Duke of Yu was going to be destroyed and left beforehand — he cannot be called unwise. When he was elevated in Qin, he knew that Duke Mu was worthy of working with and served as his minister — can that be called unwise? As minister of Qin, he made his lord illustrious throughout the realm, worthy of being remembered by later generations — could someone without talent have done this? To sell oneself in order to advance one's lord — even a self-respecting villager would not do such a thing. Would you say that a truly worthy man would?"

passages.text: 孟子曰：「伯夷，目不視惡色，耳不聽惡聲。非其君不事，非其民不使。治則進，亂則退。橫政之所出，橫民之所止，不忍居也。思與鄉人處，如以朝衣朝冠坐於塗炭也。當紂之時，居北海之濱，以待天下之清也。故聞伯夷之風者，頑夫廉，懦夫有立志。
passages.translation_en: Mencius said: "Bo Yi would not look at improper sights, nor listen to improper sounds. He would not serve a ruler he did not approve of, nor command people he did not approve of. He advanced when there was order and withdrew when there was chaos. He could not bear to dwell wherever oppressive government held sway or oppressive people resided. He thought that being among common villagers was like sitting in mud and ashes while wearing court robes and cap. During the time of the tyrant Zhou, he lived on the shores of the North Sea, waiting for the world to become pure again. Therefore, those who heard of Bo Yi's example — the greedy became incorruptible, and the cowardly found resolve."

passages.text: 「伊尹曰：『何事非君？何使非民？』治亦進，亂亦進。曰：『天之生斯民也，使先知覺後知，使先覺覺後覺。予，天民之先覺者也；予將以此道覺此民也。』思天下之民匹夫匹婦有不與被堯舜之澤者，若己推而內之溝中，其自任以天下之重也。
passages.translation_en: "Yi Yin said: 'What ruler is not worth serving? What people are not worth commanding?' He advanced whether there was order or chaos. He said: 'Heaven produced these people so that those who understand first may awaken those who understand later, and those who are awakened first may awaken those who are awakened later. I am among Heaven's people one who has been awakened first; I shall use this Way to awaken these people.' He felt that if even a single common man or woman in the world had not received the blessings of Yao and Shun, it was as if he himself had pushed them into a ditch — such was the weight of responsibility he took upon himself for the whole world."

passages.text: 「柳下惠，不羞汙君，不辭小官。進不隱賢，必以其道。遺佚而不怨，阨窮而不憫。與鄉人處，由由然不忍去也。『爾為爾，我為我，雖袒裼裸裎於我側，爾焉能浼我哉？』故聞柳下惠之風者，鄙夫寬，薄夫敦。「孔子之去齊，接淅而行；去魯，曰：『遲遲吾行也。』去父母國之道也。可以速而速，可以久而久，可以處而處，可以仕而仕，孔子也。」
passages.translation_en: "Liu Xia Hui was not ashamed to serve a corrupt ruler, nor did he consider any office too lowly. When he advanced in office, he did not hide his worthiness, and always acted according to his principles. When overlooked and passed over, he did not resent it; when impoverished and in dire straits, he did not feel sorry for himself. When among villagers, he was so easy-going and content that he could not bear to leave. He said: 'You are you and I am I. Even if you stood stripped naked at my side, how could you defile me?' Therefore, those who heard of Liu Xia Hui's example — the narrow-minded became tolerant, and the mean-spirited became generous. Confucius, when leaving Qi, grabbed the half-washed rice and departed at once. When leaving Lu, he said: 'Slowly, slowly shall I go' — this was the proper way to leave one's fatherland. When it was right to leave quickly, he left quickly; when it was right to stay long, he stayed long; when it was right to remain in retirement, he remained; when it was right to serve in office, he served. That was Confucius."

passages.text: 孟子曰：「伯夷，聖之清者也；伊尹，聖之任者也；柳下惠，聖之和者也；孔子，聖之時者也。孔子之謂集大成。集大成也者，金聲而玉振之也。金聲也者，始條理也；玉振之也者，終條理也。始條理者，智之事也；終條理者，聖之事也。智，譬則巧也；聖，譬則力也。由射於百步之外也，其至，爾力也；其中，非爾力也。」北宮錡問曰：「周室班爵祿也，如之何？」
passages.translation_en: Mencius said: "Bo Yi was the sage of purity; Yi Yin was the sage of responsibility; Liu Xia Hui was the sage of harmony; Confucius was the sage of timeliness. Confucius is what we call the complete concert. The complete concert is one in which the bells initiate and the jade chimes bring it to conclusion. The sound of the bells initiates orderly sequence; the resonance of the jade chimes concludes orderly sequence. Initiating orderly sequence is the work of wisdom; concluding orderly sequence is the work of sageness. Wisdom may be compared to skill; sageness may be compared to strength. It is like shooting from beyond a hundred paces: reaching the target depends on your strength, but hitting the mark does not depend on your strength alone." Beigong Qi asked: "How did the House of Zhou arrange its ranks and emoluments?"

passages.text: 孟子曰：「其詳不可得聞也。諸侯惡其害己也，而皆去其籍。然而軻也，嘗聞其略也。天子一位，公一位，侯一位，伯一位，子、男同一位，凡五等也。君一位，卿一位，大夫一位，上士一位，中士一位，下士一位，凡六等。「天子之制，地方千里，公侯皆方百里，伯七十里，子、男五十里，凡四等。不能五十里，不達於天子，附於諸侯，曰附庸。天子之卿受地視侯，大夫受地視伯，元士受地視子、男。
passages.translation_en: Mencius said: "The full details cannot be learned, for the feudal lords, finding the system harmful to themselves, all destroyed the records. However, I, Ke, have heard its general outline. The Son of Heaven held one rank, dukes one rank, marquises one rank, earls one rank, and viscounts and barons shared one rank — five ranks in all. The ruler held one rank, ministers one rank, grand officers one rank, senior scholars one rank, middle scholars one rank, and junior scholars one rank — six ranks in all. The Son of Heaven's domain was a thousand li square. Dukes and marquises each had a hundred li square, earls seventy li, viscounts and barons fifty li — four grades in all. Those who could not reach fifty li were not granted direct access to the Son of Heaven and were attached to a feudal lord; they were called dependencies. The Son of Heaven's ministers received land equivalent to a marquis, grand officers equivalent to an earl, and chief scholars equivalent to a viscount or baron."

passages.text: 「大國地方百里，君十卿祿，卿祿四大夫，大夫倍上士，上士倍中士，中士倍下士，下士與庶人在官者同祿，祿足以代其耕也。次國地方七十里，君十卿祿，卿祿三大夫，大夫倍上士，上士倍中士，中士倍下士，下士與庶人在官者同祿，祿足以代其耕也。小國地方五十里，君十卿祿，卿祿二大夫，大夫倍上士，上士倍中士，中士倍下士，下士與庶人在官者同祿，祿足以代其耕也。耕者之所獲，一夫百畝。百畝之糞，上農夫食九人，上次食八人，中食七人，中次食六人，下食五人。庶人在官者，其祿以是為差。」
passages.translation_en: "In a large state of a hundred li square, the ruler received ten times a minister's salary. A minister's salary was four times a grand officer's. A grand officer received double a senior scholar's, a senior scholar double a middle scholar's, a middle scholar double a junior scholar's, and a junior scholar received the same salary as a commoner employed in government service — salary sufficient to replace what he would have earned from farming. In a middle state of seventy li square, the ruler received ten times a minister's salary. A minister's salary was three times a grand officer's. A grand officer received double a senior scholar's, a senior scholar double a middle scholar's, a middle scholar double a junior scholar's, and a junior scholar received the same as a commoner in government service — salary sufficient to replace farming income. In a small state of fifty li square, the ruler received ten times a minister's salary. A minister's salary was double a grand officer's. A grand officer received double a senior scholar's, a senior scholar double a middle scholar's, a middle scholar double a junior scholar's, and a junior scholar received the same as a commoner in government service — salary sufficient to replace farming income. As for what farmers produced: one man worked a hundred mu. With proper fertilization of a hundred mu, a top-grade farmer could feed nine people, the next grade eight, a middle-grade farmer seven, the next six, and the lowest grade five. Commoners employed in government service had their salaries scaled accordingly."

passages.text: 萬章問曰：「敢問友。」
passages.translation_en: Wan Zhang asked: "May I ask about friendship?"

passages.text: 孟子曰：「不挾長，不挾貴，不挾兄弟而友。友也者，友其德也，不可以有挾也。孟獻子，百乘之家也，有友五人焉：樂正裘、牧仲，其三人，則予忘之矣。獻子之與此五人者友也，無獻子之家者也。此五人者，亦有獻子之家，則不與之友矣。非惟百乘之家為然也。雖小國之君亦有之。費惠公曰：『吾於子思，則師之矣；吾於顏般，則友之矣；王順、長息則事我者也。』非惟小國之君為然也，雖大國之君亦有之。晉平公之於亥唐也，入云則入，坐云則坐，食云則食。雖疏食菜羹，未嘗不飽，蓋不敢不飽也。然終於此而已矣。弗與共天位也，弗與治天職也，弗與食天祿也，士之尊賢者也，非王公之尊賢也。舜尚見帝，帝館甥于貳室，亦饗舜，迭為賓主，是天子而友匹夫也。用下敬上，謂之貴貴；用上敬下，謂之尊賢。貴貴、尊賢，其義一也。」
passages.translation_en: Mencius said: "In friendship, one should not rely on being older, or on being of noble rank, or on having powerful brothers. Friendship is a matter of befriending a person's virtue — there must be no leveraging of advantages. Meng Xianzi was the head of a family with a hundred chariots, and he had five friends: Yue Zheng Qiu, Mu Zhong, and three others whose names I have forgotten. Xianzi's friendship with these five men was conducted as if his family's wealth did not exist. If these five men had given weight to Xianzi's family status, they would not have been his friends. This is true not only of families with a hundred chariots. Even the ruler of a small state has such relationships. Duke Hui of Bi said: 'With Zisi I stand as a pupil before a teacher. With Yan Ban I stand as an equal friend. But Wang Shun and Chang Xi are men who serve me.' This is true not only of rulers of small states. Even rulers of great states have such relationships. Duke Ping of Jin, in his dealings with Hai Tang, entered when told to enter, sat when told to sit, and ate when told to eat. Even when it was coarse rice and vegetable broth, he always ate his fill, for he did not dare not eat his fill. Yet it went no further than this. He did not share Heaven's position with him, did not share Heaven's duties with him, did not share Heaven's emoluments with him. This was a scholar honoring a worthy man — it was not the way a king or duke honors a worthy man. When Shun went up to see Emperor Yao, Yao lodged his son-in-law in a secondary palace, and also feasted Shun, with the two of them taking turns as host and guest. This was a Son of Heaven befriending a commoner. When the lower shows deference to the higher, it is called honoring rank. When the higher shows deference to the lower, it is called honoring worth. Honoring rank and honoring worth — their principle is the same."

passages.text: 萬章問曰：「敢問交際何心也？」孟子曰：「恭也。」曰：「卻之卻之為不恭，何哉？」曰：「尊者賜之，曰『其所取之者，義乎，不義乎」，而後受之，以是為不恭，故弗卻也。」曰：「請無以辭卻之，以心卻之，曰『其取諸民之不義也』，而以他辭無受，不可乎？」曰：「其交也以道，其接也以禮，斯孔子受之矣。」萬章曰：「今有禦人於國門之外者，其交也以道，其餽也以禮，斯可受禦與？」
passages.translation_en: Wan Zhang asked: "May I ask with what attitude one should conduct social exchanges?" Mencius said: "With respect." Wan Zhang said: "Why is it that repeatedly declining a gift is considered disrespectful?" Mencius said: "When a superior bestows something, to ask 'Was the way he obtained it righteous or not?' before accepting — this is considered disrespectful, so one does not refuse." Wan Zhang said: "Suppose one does not refuse with words, but refuses in one's heart, thinking 'He took this from the people unjustly,' and then uses some other pretext not to accept. Would that not be acceptable?" Mencius said: "When the exchange is conducted according to the Way and the reception follows proper ritual, then even Confucius would have accepted." Wan Zhang said: "Suppose there is someone who robs people just outside the city gate, and his exchange follows the Way and his gift observes ritual propriety — would it be acceptable to receive stolen goods?"

passages.text: 曰：「不可。《康誥》曰：『殺越人于貨，閔不畏死，凡民罔不譈。』是不待教而誅者也。殷受夏，周受殷，所不辭也。於今為烈，如之何其受之？」曰：「今之諸侯取之於民也，猶禦也。苟善其禮際矣，斯君子受之，敢問何說也？」曰：「子以為有王者作，將比今之諸侯而誅之乎？其教之不改而後誅之乎？夫謂非其有而取之者盜也，充類至義之盡也。孔子之仕於魯也，魯人獵較，孔子亦獵較。獵較猶可，而況受其賜乎？」
passages.translation_en: Mencius said: "No, it would not. The Announcement to Kang says: 'Those who kill and rob others for their goods, fierce and fearless of death — there are none among the people who do not detest them.' Such people are to be punished without waiting to instruct them. This system was received by the Yin from the Xia, and by the Zhou from the Yin — no one disputes it. It has continued fiercely to the present day — how could one accept such gifts?" Wan Zhang said: "But today's feudal lords take from the people in ways no different from robbery. If they are scrupulous about ritual proprieties in their exchanges, then the gentleman accepts — may I ask how you explain this?" Mencius said: "Do you think that if a true king arose, he would line up all the current feudal lords and execute them? Or would he first instruct them and only execute those who refused to reform? To call it theft whenever someone takes what is not rightfully his — that is pushing the category to its logical extreme. When Confucius held office in Lu, the people of Lu were holding a competitive hunt, and Confucius also joined the competitive hunt. If even a competitive hunt was acceptable, how much more so accepting their gifts?"

passages.text: 曰：「然則孔子之仕也，非事道與？」曰：「事道也。」「事道奚獵較也？」曰：「孔子先簿正祭器，不以四方之食供簿正。」曰：「奚不去也？」曰：「為之兆也。兆足以行矣，而不行，而後去，是以未嘗有所終三年淹也。孔子有見行可之仕，有際可之仕，有公養之仕也。於季桓子，見行可之仕也；於衛靈公，際可之仕也；於衛孝公，公養之仕也。」
passages.translation_en: Wan Zhang said: "Then was Confucius's taking office not in pursuit of the Way?" Mencius said: "It was in pursuit of the Way." "If it was in pursuit of the Way, why did he join the competitive hunt?" Mencius said: "Confucius first corrected the ceremonial vessel records and would not supply the corrected records using provisions from the four quarters." "Why did he not leave?" Mencius said: "He was making a test. When the test showed that his Way could be carried out, but it was not, then he left. Thus he never stayed as long as three full years in any one place. Confucius sometimes took office because he saw his Way could be put into practice; sometimes because the reception was proper; sometimes because the ruler wished to support him. Under Ji Huan Zi, it was because he saw his Way could be practiced. Under Duke Ling of Wei, it was because the reception was proper. Under Duke Xiao of Wei, it was because the ruler wished to support him."

passages.text: 孟子曰：「仕非為貧也，而有時乎為貧；娶妻非為養也，而有時乎為養。為貧者，辭尊居卑，辭富居貧。辭尊居卑，辭富居貧，惡乎宜乎？抱關擊柝。孔子嘗為委吏矣，曰『會計當而已矣』。嘗為乘田矣，曰『牛羊茁壯，長而已矣』。位卑而言高，罪也；立乎人之本朝，而道不行，恥也」萬章曰：「士之不託諸侯，何也？」孟子曰：「不敢也。諸侯失國，而後託於諸侯，禮也；士之託於諸侯，非禮也。」萬章曰：「君餽之粟，則受之乎？」
passages.translation_en: Mencius said: "Taking office is not for the sake of poverty, yet sometimes it is because of poverty. Marrying a wife is not for the sake of having someone to care for one's parents, yet sometimes it is for that reason. One who takes office because of poverty should decline high rank and remain in a low position, decline wealth and remain in poverty. What position would be appropriate for such a person? A gatekeeper or a night watchman. Confucius once served as a minor official in charge of stores, and he said: 'My accounts are accurate — that is all that matters.' He once served as an overseer of livestock, and he said: 'The cattle and sheep are thriving and well-grown — that is all that matters.' To hold a low position and speak of lofty matters is a transgression. To stand in a ruler's court while one's Way is not practiced is a disgrace." Wan Zhang said: "Why does a scholar not depend on feudal lords for his livelihood?" Mencius said: "He does not dare to. When a feudal lord has lost his state, it is proper for him to depend on another feudal lord. But for a scholar to depend on a feudal lord is not proper." Wan Zhang said: "If the ruler sends him grain, should he accept it?"

passages.text: 曰：「受之。」「受之何義也？」曰：「君之於氓也，固周之。」曰：「周之則受，賜之則不受，何也？」曰：「不敢也。」曰：「敢問其不敢何也？」曰：「抱關擊柝者，皆有常職以食於上。無常職而賜於上者，以為不恭也。」曰：「君餽之，則受之，不識可常繼乎？」
passages.translation_en: Mencius said: "He should accept it." "On what principle does he accept it?" "A ruler naturally provides relief to those who dwell in his territory." "He accepts relief but not gifts — why?" "He does not dare." "May I ask why he does not dare?" "Gatekeepers and night watchmen all have a regular office through which they receive sustenance from their superiors. To receive sustenance from one's superiors without holding a regular office is considered disrespectful." "If the ruler sends grain, he accepts it — but may this continue indefinitely?"

passages.text: 曰：「繆公之於子思也，亟問，亟餽鼎肉。子思不悅。於卒也，摽使者出諸大門之外，北面稽首再拜而不受。曰：『今而後知君之犬馬畜伋。』蓋自是臺無餽也。悅賢不能舉，又不能養也，可謂悅賢乎？」曰：「敢問國君欲養君子，如何斯可謂養矣？」
passages.translation_en: Mencius said: "Duke Mu of Lu, in his dealings with Zisi, sent frequent inquiries and frequent gifts of cauldrons of meat. Zisi was displeased. Finally, he ushered the messenger out through the main gate, bowed to the north, kowtowed twice, and refused the gift, saying: 'Now I realize that the ruler keeps me, Si, as he would keep a dog or horse.' From then on, no more gifts were sent. When one claims to delight in a worthy man but can neither promote him nor properly support him, can that truly be called delighting in a worthy man?" Wan Zhang said: "May I ask how a ruler should support a gentleman so that it can properly be called support?"

passages.text: 曰：「以君命將之，再拜稽首而受。其後廩人繼粟，庖人繼肉，不以君命將之。子思以為鼎肉，使己僕僕爾亟拜也，非養君子之道也。堯之於舜也，使其子九男事之，二女女焉，百官牛羊倉廩備，以養舜於畎畝之中，後舉而加諸上位。故曰：王公之尊賢者也。」萬章曰：「敢問不見諸侯，何義也？」孟子曰：「在國曰市井之臣，在野曰草莽之臣，皆謂庶人。庶人不傳質為臣，不敢見於諸侯，禮也。」
passages.translation_en: Mencius said: "The gift should be presented with a formal command from the ruler, and the recipient bows twice, kowtows, and accepts. After that, the granary keeper delivers grain and the cook delivers meat on a regular basis, without each delivery requiring a formal command from the ruler. Zisi felt that having cauldrons of meat delivered with ceremony each time, forcing him to bow and kowtow repeatedly, was not the proper way to support a gentleman. When Yao dealt with Shun, he had his nine sons serve Shun, gave two of his daughters in marriage to him, and provided officials, cattle, sheep, and storehouses to support Shun amid the fields — and only afterward raised him to the highest position. Therefore this is called 'the way a king or duke honors a worthy man.'" Wan Zhang said: "May I ask on what principle a man does not go to see the feudal lords?" Mencius said: "One who lives in the city is called a subject of the marketplace. One who lives in the countryside is called a subject of the wilds. Both are commoners. A commoner who has not presented the ceremonial gift to become a subject does not dare appear before the feudal lord — that is proper ritual."

passages.text: 萬章曰：「庶人，召之役，則往役；君欲見之，召之，則不往見之，何也？」曰：「往役，義也；往見，不義也。且君之欲見之也，何為也哉？」曰：「為其多聞也，為其賢也。」
passages.translation_en: Wan Zhang said: "A commoner, when summoned to perform labor service, goes. But when the ruler wishes to see him and summons him, he does not go — why is that?" Mencius said: "Going to perform labor service is a duty. Going for an audience is not a duty. Besides, why does the ruler wish to see him?" Wan Zhang said: "Because of his wide learning, because of his worthiness."

passages.text: 曰：「為其多聞也，則天子不召師，而況諸侯乎？為其賢也，則吾未聞欲見賢而召之也。繆公亟見於子思，曰：『古千乘之國以友士，何如？』子思不悅，曰：『古之人有言：曰事之云乎，豈曰友之云乎？』子思之不悅也，豈不曰：『以位，則子，君也；我，臣也。何敢與君友也？以德，則子事我者也。奚可以與我友？』千乘之君求與之友，而不可得也，而況可召與？齊景公田，招虞人以旌，不至，將殺之。志士不忘在溝壑，勇士不忘喪其元。孔子奚取焉？取非其招不往也。」
passages.translation_en: Mencius said: "If it is because of his wide learning, then even the Son of Heaven does not summon his teacher — how much less should a feudal lord? If it is because of his worthiness, then I have never heard of wanting to see a worthy man by summoning him. Duke Mu of Lu frequently went to see Zisi and said: 'In ancient times, how did rulers of states with a thousand chariots befriend scholars?' Zisi was displeased and said: 'The ancients had a saying — they spoke of serving them, not of befriending them!' Zisi's displeasure meant: 'In terms of rank, you are the ruler and I am the subject — how dare I presume to be your friend? In terms of virtue, you should be serving me — how can you presume to be my friend?' If the ruler of a state with a thousand chariots sought friendship with Zisi and could not obtain it, how much less could he summon him? Duke Jing of Qi was hunting and summoned his gamekeeper with a pennant. The gamekeeper did not come, and the Duke was about to have him killed. 'A man of resolve never forgets he may end up in a ditch. A brave man never forgets he may lose his head.' What did Confucius find admirable in this? He admired the fact that the gamekeeper would not go when summoned by the wrong signal."

passages.text: 曰：「敢問招虞人何以？」曰：「以皮冠。庶人以旃，士以旂，大夫以旌。以大夫之招招虞人，虞人死不敢往。以士之招招庶人，庶人豈敢往哉。況乎以不賢人之招招賢人乎？欲見賢人而不以其道，猶欲其入而閉之門也。夫義，路也；禮，門也。惟君子能由是路，出入是門也。《詩》云：『周道如砥，其直如矢；君子所履，小人所視。』」萬章曰：「孔子，君命召，不俟駕而行。然則孔子非與？」曰：「孔子當仕有官職，而以其官召之也。」
passages.translation_en: Wan Zhang said: "May I ask, what is the proper way to summon a gamekeeper?" Mencius said: "With a leather cap. A commoner is summoned with a plain banner, a scholar with a dragon-and-snake banner, a grand officer with a feathered pennant. When a gamekeeper was summoned with the signal meant for a grand officer, the gamekeeper would rather die than go. When a commoner is summoned with the signal meant for a scholar, how would the commoner dare go? How much worse is it to summon a worthy man with the signal meant for an unworthy man! Wanting to see a worthy man but not following the proper way is like wanting him to enter while keeping the door shut. Righteousness is the road; ritual is the door. Only a gentleman can travel this road and pass through this door. The Book of Songs says: 'The highways of Zhou are smooth as a whetstone, straight as an arrow. They are what the gentleman treads, and what the common people gaze upon.'" Wan Zhang said: "When Confucius received a summons from his ruler, he set out without waiting for his carriage to be yoked. Was Confucius then wrong?" Mencius said: "Confucius was then holding office with official duties, and he was summoned in his capacity as an officeholder."

passages.text: 孟子謂萬章曰：「一鄉之善士，斯友一鄉之善士；一國之善士，斯友一國之善士；天下之善士，斯友天下之善士。以友天下之善士為未足，又尚論古之人。頌其詩，讀其書，不知其人，可乎？是以論其世也。是尚友也。」齊宣王問卿。孟子曰：「王何卿之問也？」王曰：「卿不同乎？」曰：「不同。有貴戚之卿，有異姓之卿。」王曰：「請問貴戚之卿。」曰：「君有大過則諫，反覆之而不聽，則易位。」
passages.translation_en: Mencius said to Wan Zhang: "The best scholar in a village befriends the best scholars in the village. The best scholar in a state befriends the best scholars in the state. The best scholar in the world befriends the best scholars in the world. And when befriending all the best scholars in the world is not enough, he goes further and considers the ancients. He recites their poems and reads their writings — but can he do so without knowing who they were as persons? Therefore he studies their times as well. This is what it means to seek friends upward through history." King Xuan of Qi asked about ministers. Mencius said: "What kind of ministers is the King asking about?" The King said: "Are ministers not all the same?" Mencius said: "They are not. There are ministers who are royal kinsmen, and ministers of a different surname." The King said: "May I ask about ministers who are royal kinsmen?" Mencius said: "If the ruler commits great faults, they remonstrate. If he repeatedly refuses to listen, they replace him."

passages.text: 王勃然變乎色。曰：「王勿異也。王問臣，臣不敢不以正對。」王色定，然後請問異姓之卿。曰：「君有過則諫，反覆之而不聽，則去。」
passages.translation_en: The King flushed with anger. Mencius said: "Let the King not take this amiss. The King asked his minister, and his minister dares not answer with anything but the truth." When the King's expression calmed, he asked about ministers of a different surname. Mencius said: "If the ruler commits faults, they remonstrate. If he repeatedly refuses to listen, they leave."

passages.text: 告子曰：「性，猶杞柳也；義，猶桮棬也。以人性為仁義，猶以杞柳為桮棬。」孟子曰：「子能順杞柳之性而以為桮棬乎？將戕賊杞柳而後以為桮棬也？如將戕賊杞柳而以為桮棬，則亦將戕賊人以為仁義與？率天下之人而禍仁義者，必子之言夫！」告子曰：「性猶湍水也，決諸東方則東流，決諸西方則西流。人性之無分於善不善也，猶水之無分於東西也。」
passages.translation_en: Gaozi said: "Human nature is like willow wood; righteousness is like cups and bowls. To make human nature into benevolence and righteousness is like making willow wood into cups and bowls." Mencius said: "Can you follow the natural grain of willow wood to make cups and bowls? Or must you mutilate and damage the willow before making them into cups and bowls? If you must mutilate the willow to make cups and bowls, then must you also mutilate people to make them benevolent and righteous? It is your words that will lead everyone in the world to bring disaster upon benevolence and righteousness!" Gaozi said: "Human nature is like swirling water. Open a channel to the east and it flows east; open a channel to the west and it flows west. Human nature does not distinguish between good and not good, just as water does not distinguish between east and west."

passages.text: 孟子曰：「水信無分於東西。無分於上下乎？人性之善也，猶水之就下也。人無有不善，水無有不下。今夫水，搏而躍之，可使過顙；激而行之，可使在山。是豈水之性哉？其勢則然也。人之可使為不善，其性亦猶是也。」告子曰：「生之謂性。」孟子曰：「生之謂性也，猶白之謂白與？」曰：「然。」「白羽之白也，猶白雪之白；白雪之白，猶白玉之白與？」曰：「然。」「然則犬之性，猶牛之性；牛之性，猶人之性與？」
passages.translation_en: Mencius said: "Water indeed does not distinguish between east and west. But does it not distinguish between up and down? The goodness of human nature is like water's tendency to flow downward. There is no person who is not good, just as there is no water that does not flow downward. Now, if you strike water and splash it up, you can make it leap over your forehead; if you dam it and force it along, you can make it stay on a mountain. But is this the nature of water? It is the force of circumstances that makes it so. That people can be made to do what is not good—their nature is treated in just the same way." Gaozi said: "What is inborn is what we call nature." Mencius said: "When you say what is inborn is nature, is that like saying white is white?" Gaozi said: "Yes." "Then is the whiteness of white feathers the same as the whiteness of white snow, and the whiteness of white snow the same as the whiteness of white jade?" "Yes." "Then is the nature of a dog the same as the nature of an ox, and the nature of an ox the same as the nature of a human being?"

passages.text: 告子曰：「食色，性也。仁，內也，非外也；義，外也，非內也。」孟子曰：「何以謂仁內義外也？」曰：「彼長而我長之，非有長於我也；猶彼白而我白之，從其白於外也，故謂之外也。」曰：「異於白馬之白也，無以異於白人之白也；不識長馬之長也，無以異於長人之長與？且謂長者義乎？長之者義乎？」曰：「吾弟則愛之，秦人之弟則不愛也，是以我為悅者也，故謂之內。長楚人之長，亦長吾之長，是以長為悅者也，故謂之外也。」
passages.translation_en: Gaozi said: "The appetite for food and sex—that is human nature. Benevolence is internal, not external; righteousness is external, not internal." Mencius said: "Why do you say benevolence is internal and righteousness is external?" Gaozi said: "When someone is older and I treat him as an elder, it is not because there is something elder-like in me. It is like when something is white and I call it white—I am responding to the whiteness outside me. That is why I call it external." Mencius said: "The whiteness of a white horse is no different from the whiteness of a white person; but is respecting an old horse the same as respecting an old person? And which do you call righteousness—the fact that someone is old, or the act of treating them as an elder?" Gaozi said: "My own younger brother I love, but a man of Qin's younger brother I do not love. This is because I am the one who feels the pleasure, so I call it internal. I treat an elder of Chu as an elder, just as I treat my own elder as an elder. This is because the elderliness is what pleases me, so I call it external."

passages.text: 曰：「耆秦人之炙，無以異於耆吾炙。夫物則亦有然者也，然則耆炙亦有外與？」孟季子問公都子曰：「何以謂義內也？」曰：「行吾敬，故謂之內也。」「鄉人長於伯兄一歲，則誰敬？」曰：「敬兄。」「酌則誰先？」曰：「先酌鄉人。」「所敬在此，所長在彼，果在外，非由內也。」
passages.translation_en: Mencius said: "Our enjoyment of a man of Qin's roast meat is no different from our enjoyment of our own roast meat. Things can be like this too. So is the enjoyment of roast meat also external?" Meng Jizi asked Gongduzi: "Why do you say righteousness is internal?" Gongduzi said: "I am acting on my own feeling of respect, so I call it internal." "If a fellow villager is one year older than your eldest brother, whom do you show respect to?" "I show respect to my brother." "But when pouring wine, whom do you serve first?" "I serve the villager first." "Your real respect is directed at one person, but the honor you show goes to another. So it is determined by external circumstances, not from within."

passages.text: 公都子不能答，以告孟子。孟子曰：「敬叔父乎？敬弟乎？彼將曰『敬叔父』。曰：『弟為尸，則誰敬？』彼將曰『敬弟。』子曰：『惡在其敬叔父也？』彼將曰『在位故也。』子亦曰：『在位故也。庸敬在兄，斯須之敬在鄉人。』」季子聞之曰：「敬叔父則敬，敬弟則敬，果在外，非由內也。」公都子曰：「冬日則飲湯，夏日則飲水，然則飲食亦在外也？」
passages.translation_en: Gongduzi could not answer, and reported this to Mencius. Mencius said: "Ask him: 'Do you respect your uncle, or your younger brother?' He will say, 'My uncle.' Then say: 'If your younger brother is serving as the ceremonial impersonator of the dead, then whom do you respect?' He will say, 'My younger brother.' Then you ask: 'What happened to your respect for your uncle?' He will say: 'It is because of the position my brother holds.' Then you can likewise say: 'It is because of the position the villager holds. Ordinary respect belongs to the elder brother; temporary, situational respect goes to the villager.'" When Jizi heard this, he said: "When I respect my uncle, it is respect; when I respect my younger brother, it is also respect. So it really is determined by external circumstances, not from within." Gongduzi said: "In winter we drink hot water; in summer we drink cold water. Then is eating and drinking also determined by external circumstances?"

passages.text: 公都子曰：「告子曰：『性無善無不善也。』或曰：『性可以為善，可以為不善；是故文武興，則民好善；幽厲興，則民好暴。』或曰：『有性善，有性不善；是故以堯為君而有象，以瞽瞍為父而有舜；以紂為兄之子且以為君，而有微子啟、王子比干。』今曰『性善』，然則彼皆非與？」
passages.translation_en: Gongduzi said: "Gaozi says: 'Human nature is neither good nor not good.' Others say: 'Human nature can be made good or not good. That is why when Kings Wen and Wu arose, the people were inclined toward goodness; when Kings You and Li arose, the people were inclined toward cruelty.' Still others say: 'Some natures are good and some are not good. That is why even with Yao as sovereign there was Xiang; even with the Blind Man as father there was Shun; and even with the tyrant Zhou as nephew and sovereign, there were Viscount Wei of Qi and Prince Bigan.' Now you say human nature is good—are all these others wrong?"

passages.text: 孟子曰：「乃若其情，則可以為善矣，乃所謂善也。若夫為不善，非才之罪也。惻隱之心，人皆有之；羞惡之心，人皆有之；恭敬之心，人皆有之；是非之心，人皆有之。惻隱之心，仁也；羞惡之心，義也；恭敬之心，禮也；是非之心，智也。仁義禮智，非由外鑠我也，我固有之也，弗思耳矣。故曰：『求則得之，舍則失之。』或相倍蓰而無算者，不能盡其才者也。《詩》曰：『天生蒸民，有物有則。民之秉夷，好是懿德。』孔子曰：『為此詩者，其知道乎！故有物必有則，民之秉夷也，故好是懿德。』」
passages.translation_en: Mencius said: "As far as our natural feelings are concerned, we are capable of being good. That is what I mean by calling human nature good. As for those who do what is not good, that is not the fault of their native endowment. The feeling of compassion—all people have it. The feeling of shame and disgust—all people have it. The feeling of respect and reverence—all people have it. The feeling of right and wrong—all people have it. The feeling of compassion is benevolence. The feeling of shame is righteousness. The feeling of respect is propriety. The feeling of right and wrong is wisdom. Benevolence, righteousness, propriety, and wisdom are not welded onto us from outside—we inherently possess them. It is simply that we do not reflect upon this. Therefore it is said: 'Seek and you will find them; neglect and you will lose them.' That people differ from one another by twice, five times, or even incalculably—that is because they cannot fully develop their native endowment. The Book of Odes says: 'Heaven gave birth to the multitudes of people; where there are things, there are standards. The people's constant nature is to love admirable virtue.' Confucius said: 'The one who wrote this poem truly understood the Way! Therefore where there are things there must be standards, and because the people hold to their constant nature, they love admirable virtue.'"

passages.text: 孟子曰：「富歲，子弟多賴；凶歲，子弟多暴，非天之降才爾殊也，其所以陷溺其心者然也。今夫麰麥，播種而耰之，其地同，樹之時又同，浡然而生，至於日至之時，皆熟矣。雖有不同，則地有肥磽，雨露之養，人事之不齊也。故凡同類者，舉相似也，何獨至於人而疑之？聖人與我同類者。故龍子曰：『不知足而為屨，我知其不為蕢也。』屨之相似，天下之足同也。口之於味，有同耆也。易牙先得我口之所耆者也。如使口之於味也，其性與人殊，若犬馬之與我不同類也，則天下何耆皆從易牙之於味也？至於味，天下期於易牙，是天下之口相似也惟耳亦然。至於聲，天下期於師曠，是天下之耳相似也。惟目亦然。至於子都，天下莫不知其姣也。不知子都之姣者，無目者也。故曰：口之於味也，有同耆焉；耳之於聲也，有同聽焉；目之於色也，有同美焉。至於心，獨無所同然乎？心之所同然者何也？謂理也，義也。聖人先得我心之所同然耳。故理義之悅我心，猶芻豢之悅我口。」
passages.translation_en: Mencius said: "In good harvest years, young men are mostly easygoing; in bad harvest years, young men are mostly violent.
